- a comma or a dot before the milliseconds, the `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and any number of fraction digits
- position settings after the end time, which are ignored
- `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>` and `<font>` tags and `{\an8}`-style overrides, which are removed, plus the common HTML entities (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `'`, ` `)
- text in UTF-8, UTF-16, Windows-1252 or Latin-1

The file's own line breaks are kept. Long lines also wrap inside the caption box.

**Malformed entries are reported, not dropped silently.** If a block has no `-->` timing line, has a time that cannot be read, ends at or before its start, or has no text, it is skipped. When the import finishes, an alert lists what was skipped by line number (the first eight, then "…and N more"), along with how many captions were shortened to fit. A clean import shows no alert. A file in which no cue can be read is refused, and the message gives the first few reasons.

*Agents:* `import_captions` (`path`, plus an optional existing `track`; reports what landed and, under `skipped`, each malformed entry by line).

## Generate captions from speech

Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. The item is greyed out when nothing in the project can be transcribed. Playback pauses and the **Generate Captions** sheet opens. It is one card: you set it up, press **Generate**, and the same card becomes the progress bar. The footnote reads "captions go on a new track".

### What can be transcribed

A clip can be transcribed only if it plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track, its audio is switched on, and its file is present. Clips that cannot be transcribed are skipped with a reason:

- its source is not a media file (text, shape, still, image, graphic or nest)
- it plays in reverse
- its media has no audio track
- its audio is switched off (for example, the picture half of a clip after Detach Audio, whose sound is on the audio-only clip below it)
- its media file is missing
- its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it
- its speed or length is degenerate

Captions follow a clip's speed. On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it is heard on the timeline ([Speed](speed.md)). They keep following it afterwards: change the speed or a ramp of a clip with sound and the captions over it move with its speech in the same undo step ([Speed](speed.md#captions-follow-a-speed-change)).

### The sheet

| Row | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Language** | The spoken language. With **On this Mac**, every language this Mac's recogniser supports; a language whose model is not installed reads "— not installed". With **AssemblyAI**, **Detect automatically** and then 21 languages. | On this Mac: your Mac's own language. AssemblyAI: Detect automatically. |
| *(Download row)* | Appears when the chosen on-device language is not installed. See below. | — |
| **Engine** | **On this Mac** or **AssemblyAI**. | The engine you chose last time; On this Mac the first time. |
| **Speakers** | AssemblyAI only. "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles". | Off |
| **Vocabulary** | AssemblyAI only. Names and jargon to expect, separated by commas. | Empty |
| **Transcribe again** | AssemblyAI only. "ignore any cached transcript" uploads again even when a usable transcript is cached. | Off |
| **From** | **Selected clips**, **In/out range** or **Whole timeline**. A choice that holds nothing transcribable is greyed. **In/out range** takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. | Selected clips if the selection holds anything transcribable, else In/out range if one is marked, else Whole timeline. |
| **Style** | **Subtitles** or one of the five word caption styles. See [Caption styles](#caption-styles). | The style you chose last time; Subtitles the first time. |
| *(looks)* | **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken**, **Dim in pauses**. See [Looks](#looks-for-word-captions). | Each one as you last left it; off the first time. |
| *(preview)* | A sample page drawn at this canvas's size. | — |
| **Replace** | "existing captions" swaps out earlier caption tracks over the same clips. See [Restyle a caption track](#restyle-a-caption-track). | Off |

The **Speakers**, **Vocabulary** and **Transcribe again** rows are hidden, not greyed, while Engine is **On this Mac**. They appear when you choose **AssemblyAI**.

Under the grid, a summary line gives the clip count and the length of audio (for example, `3 clips · 00:04:12.000 of audio`) or "Nothing to transcribe". Under the summary is a note explaining anything that is stopping the run. **Generate** is live only when the run can go ahead.

### On this Mac

The hint at the top of the sheet reads: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."

Each clip's own part of its media is extracted and recognised locally. There is no permission prompt and no length limit. Nothing is cached for captions on this Mac: every run, restyling included, recognises the audio again. That is free, but it takes the time again. The sheet's preview never uses on-device words.

**Installing a language.** Speech models are installed per Mac. If you choose a language marked "— not installed", a **Download** button appears below the Language popup, and **Generate** stays greyed until the model is in. While the download runs, the row shows "Downloading *language*… N%", the button becomes **Cancel**, and the Language and Engine popups are locked. The row shows a percentage, not a size, because the size isn't known before the download starts. When it finishes, the language is installed and selected. If the download fails, the note says why. This button is the only place a model is ever downloaded.

If this Mac's recogniser lists no language at all, the popup reads "No on-device language", and the note asks you to reopen the sheet to check again.

### With AssemblyAI

The hint reads: "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (*region*), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." *Region* is **United States** or **European Union**, whichever is set in Settings.

**You need** an AssemblyAI API key, saved in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,) under **Transcription** ([below](#your-assemblyai-key)). Without one, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set — Frame Job ▸ Settings…" and **Generate** is greyed (unless every file is already cached; see below). If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable. An untitled project can be transcribed too: its transcripts are kept in a temporary folder until the project is saved, and then go into the project package.

**What is uploaded.** The audio of every media file behind the chosen clips is uploaded, and it is the whole file, not just the parts the clips use. AssemblyAI bills for the whole file, so a long recording that you use only briefly still costs its full length. A single file longer than 10 hours is refused before anything is sent: "“*name*” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file."

**The price, before you press Generate.** The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, for example:

`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`

The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers** on, as published on 2026-09-17. A very short run is priced "under $0.01". When every file is already cached, the line starts "Nothing to upload", for example `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.

Hover over the summary to see the reason for each file, such as "has not been transcribed yet", "has changed since it was transcribed", "was transcribed with a different language", "was transcribed for a different request" or "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for", followed by the rate sentence. Two other counts can appear: a file "waiting on an earlier delete", which this run will not upload, and a file that "could not be read". A waiting file's hover line gives the price it would add: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $X more if it does."

**The transcript cache.** Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package and reused by the next run. A file whose cached transcript matches the request (same file, model, language, Speakers and Vocabulary) is not uploaded again and costs nothing. The caption style does not count, so restyling never uploads. A transcript made for Remove Filler Words also serves Generate Captions, so that file is not uploaded or billed again. The cache is kept per media entry, so two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately. When no API key is set and every file in the run already has a current transcript, the hint changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." and **Generate** works without a key. With a key set, the usual hint stays, and the summary says there is nothing to upload. To force a fresh upload anyway, tick **Transcribe again**.

**Filler words.** AssemblyAI's words include fillers such as um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, er and erm. Captions, and the sheet's preview, leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them.

**Deletion at AssemblyAI.** Once the words have been read back, Frame Job asks AssemblyAI to delete its copy. If AssemblyAI does not confirm the delete, the result says so:

- Normally the delete is retried at the next run that has a key for the same account and region the transcript was made in.
- If no key is set when that next run starts, the result says cleanup was deferred because no API key is set.
- If the transcript could not be kept in the project, Frame Job has no record to retry from, and the result reads "…Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard."

While a delete is pending, that file is not uploaded again. Its current cached transcript is still used, but **Transcribe again** is refused for it until the delete goes through.

**Speakers.** With **Speakers** ticked, a change of speaker always starts a new cue or page. In the **Subtitles** style, each speaker's cues take their own colour, in the order the speakers first appear: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. Speakers are counted separately for each media file.

**Vocabulary.** Type the words and phrases to expect, such as product names, people and identifiers, separated by commas. Blank entries and repeats are dropped (the first spelling is kept), and the list is capped at 1,000 terms. If the cap cuts your list, the note says "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."

**Languages.** Detect automatically, English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish and Vietnamese.

### Progress and the result

While a run is going, the card shows a progress bar, "Transcribing N clips…" ("…with AssemblyAI…" for the cloud), and a detail line. On this Mac, the detail is the clip being recognised. With AssemblyAI, it is the current stage: "Extracting *file*", "Uploading *file* · 12 MB of 40", "Submitting *file*", "Waiting for AssemblyAI · 35 s", "Saving *file*". **Cancel** stops the run, and closing the sheet mid-run also stops it. After Cancel, the detail line reads "Stopping…" until the run ends, and nothing is placed.

If one file cannot be transcribed, its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. With AssemblyAI, a key that AssemblyAI refuses ends the run straight away, so no more files are uploaded.

Placing the captions is one undo step, **Generate Captions**. A clean run closes the sheet by itself. If there is something to report, the card stays open with **Close**, saying how many captions were added on which track, how many were shortened, which clips were skipped and why, and any of these from a cloud run:

- a file transcribed with a fallback model instead of Universal-3.5 Pro
- with **Detect automatically**: the language detected for each file and how confident AssemblyAI was, for example "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)"
- a delete AssemblyAI has not confirmed, or a transcript that could not be kept in the project

A failure shows the error on the same card.

*Agents:* `transcribe`. It takes `clips` (the scope), `engine` (`apple`, the default, or `assemblyai`), `language` (`auto` by default with AssemblyAI), `style`, `replace`, `slide`, `fill`, `dim`, and, for AssemblyAI only, `speakers`, `vocabulary` and `refresh`, each refused by name without `engine: "assemblyai"`. It answers the cues in timeline ticks (with each word's timing for a word style) whether or not it places them, and `place: false` changes nothing at all. `replace` is refused with `subtitles` or with `place: false`; when it is given, a placed run lists the removed tracks' ids under `replaced`. The tool never remembers the sheet's engine, style or looks, and never downloads a language model. A language whose model is not installed is refused by name.

## Subtitles

The **Subtitles** style makes classic two-line cues, built by these rules:

- at most two lines of at most 42 characters each
- at most 6 seconds per cue
- at least one frame between cues
- never two speakers in one cue

A word too long for a line is left whole rather than hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.

Each cue uses the **Caption** text preset: Source Sans 3 Regular at 3.5% of the canvas height, centred, on a 60% black backdrop, wrapping at 80% of the canvas width, with its box centred 38% of the frame height below the middle.

## Caption styles

The five word caption styles make the large, one-row captions used in shorts and reels. Instead of a cue, each clip holds a **page** of words with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. All five are white with the spoken word marked. They are sized to the shorter side of the canvas, so a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height.

| Style | Typeface | Case | How the spoken word shows | Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Subtitles** | Source Sans 3 Regular | As written | — (two-line cues, above) | 38% of the frame height below centre |
| **Highlight** | Montserrat Black, black outline | UPPERCASE | Turns yellow and pops to 112% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **Pill** | Montserrat ExtraBold | UPPERCASE | Sits on a violet pill | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **Karaoke** | Montserrat ExtraBold | As written | Words turn yellow as they are said and stay yellow; words still to come are dimmed white. Up to two lines | 28% of the frame height below centre |
| **Build** | Anton, black outline | UPPERCASE | Words appear one by one; the newest is yellow and pops to 115% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
| **One Word** | Bebas Neue, black outline | UPPERCASE | One large word at a time, popping to 120% | 18% of the frame height below centre |

The text is 7.5% of the shorter canvas side, and 12% for One Word. The four display faces ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License.

### How pages are filled

A page is filled to the width it actually measures in its style on your canvas, not to a word count:

- A page fills up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line (Karaoke: up to two).
- It ends early at a pause of 0.25 s or more, after a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`, after 3 seconds on screen, or at a change of speaker. One Word pages hold one word each.
- A comma, semicolon or colon just before the width runs out moves the break back to it, if the page is already at least half full.
- A single word too wide for the frame shrinks, down to 80% of the style's size, before it wraps.
- A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page when the gap is under 0.25 s, so the row does not blink between pages.
- Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.

### The preview

The preview under the Style row shows a sample page drawn by the same renderer the canvas uses, at this canvas's proportions. It uses the first words of the first clip's cached transcript when there is one, and "This is how it looks" otherwise. A word style shows two frames, with the first word active and then the second. A ticked **Fill words as spoken** shows the fill half done, and a ticked **Slide the pill** shows the pill half-way through its slide. **Dim in pauses** is not previewed.

## Looks for word captions

Three checkboxes under the Style popup each add a look to a word style's pages. Each is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs. A box that does not apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but keeps its tick for when you switch back.

| Look | What it does | Works with |
|---|---|---|
| **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, over 0.2 s (or less when the next word comes sooner), instead of jumping. | Pill |
| **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it is spoken, taking at most 0.6 s. The part already said is in the highlight colour; the rest is in the upcoming colour (Karaoke's dimmed white), or not yet drawn in Build. | Highlight, Karaoke, Build |
| **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. It also dims before the first word when that word starts late, and after the last word until the caption ends. Each fade takes 0.1 s. | All five word styles |

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.

*Agents:* `transcribe`'s `slide`, `fill` and `dim`. Each is false unless given, never what the sheet last chose. `true` is refused by name with a style it would not show on, or with `place: false`; `false` is always accepted. A placed run given any of the three lists the looks that were on under `looks`.

## Restyle a caption track

A style is fixed when the captions are generated. To change it, generate again with **Replace** ticked:

1. Open **File ▸ Generate Captions…** over the same clips.
2. Choose the new word style and looks.
3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
4. Press **Generate**.

The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front, all in one undo step. With AssemblyAI the cached transcript is reused, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed.

**Replace** is live only for a word style, and only when there is a track it may replace. That means a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. Tracks outside the run's scope are left alone.

## Editing captions

Captions are text clips, so the inspector's Clip tab edits them under **Text**: Content, Font, Style, Outline, Backdrop, Box, Reveal and Presets. Select several captions to change them together.

On a word caption page:

- **Case.** The style's capitals come from **Text ▸ Style ▸ UPPERCASE**. Untick it to show a page as written. Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the Content box shows the words as written, and changing case never drops the word timing.
- **Word style colours.** There is no inspector section for a page's word style (highlight colour, pop scale, pill colour). To change them, generate again with a different style, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
- **Editing the words.** Changing the text while keeping the same number of words keeps every word's timing. Changing the number of words drops the timing, and the page then shows plainly. The Content section notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". The same rule holds whether you edit in the Content box or in place on the canvas (double-click the page).
- **Reveal.** The text reveals (typewriter, word fade, line rise) do not apply to a timed page. The Reveal section says "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
- **Trimming and splitting.** These keep each word on the speech it times. Retiming a page by dragging it moves its words with it.

*Agents:* `set_text` edits a caption like any text clip, including a page's `words` and `word_style`. When `words` is not empty, it must have exactly one timing for each word of the content. Otherwise the edit is refused: "this text is timed word by word: N timings for M words".

## Export captions

Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. The item is greyed out unless some track holds only text clips with caption text on them. The save panel suggests *project name*`.srt` and adds two popups:

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Track** | Which track to write, listed as "*name* — N cues (track *id*)", front-most first. Greyed when there is only one candidate. | The front-most candidate |
| **Format** | **SubRip (.srt)** or **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Changing it changes the file name's extension. | SubRip (.srt) |

Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now, so a caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Empty captions are left out. Line endings become LF, and blank lines inside a caption are removed. The two formats differ only in WebVTT's `WEBVTT` header, its missing index lines, the `.` where SubRip writes `,` in timestamps, and WebVTT escaping `&`, `<` and `>`. Exporting changes nothing in the project.

Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips can be exported, a titles track included. A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written: the style's UPPERCASE, its word timings and its styling are not part of a `.srt` or `.vtt`.

**Round trips are exact to the frame.** A track exported and imported again puts every cue back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match byte for byte, because import snaps times to the frame grid: at 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`.

*Agents:* `export_captions` (`path`, plus optional `track` and `format`). The track is never guessed: with no candidate, or more than one and no `track` given, the call is refused and the candidates are listed. A `.srt` or `.vtt` extension in `path` is replaced by the format's own, and any other extension is kept (`chart.png` becomes `chart.png.srt`).

## Your AssemblyAI key

The key lives in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,), in the **Transcription** section:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. "Paste your key" when none is saved. A saved key shows as a fixed row of dots and is never displayed again. Press Return or **Save** to save. |
| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**: the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to. Default: United States. The two regions do not share transcripts, so a pending delete is retried only in the region it was made in. |
| **Save** | Saves the key typed in the field ("Key saved."). |
| **Remove** | Deletes the saved key ("Key removed."). Live only when a key is saved. |
| **Verify** | Makes the cheapest signed-in call to AssemblyAI with the key in the field, or the saved key, and answers "Key accepted" or AssemblyAI's reason. It reads "Checking…" while it runs, "No API key is set." with no key, and "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." if the key or region changes mid-check. It does not transcribe or bill anything. |
| **Account Page** | Opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in the browser, where you get a key and see your spending. |

The key is saved in a file only you can read (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`, mode `0600`), not in the Keychain, and it is never passed on the command line. Saving, removing or changing the region updates an open Generate Captions sheet straight away. The ⓘ beside the heading explains what is uploaded, what is deleted, and the published rate.

No MCP tool can read or change the key or the region. Only a person sets them, here.

## Limits

- **Import reads SubRip only.** WebVTT can be exported but not imported.
- Captions are burned-in text clips, not a switchable subtitle stream in the exported movie.
- A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio switched off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent cannot be transcribed.
- **On this Mac** needs the language's speech model installed from the sheet's Download row. Speakers, Vocabulary and Transcribe again are AssemblyAI only.
- **AssemblyAI** needs a key (unless every file is already cached), uploads and bills each whole media file, and refuses a file over 10 hours. Vocabulary is capped at 1,000 terms.
- Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
- Word styles mark words by their timing only. There is no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
- A page's word style colours and scale cannot be edited in the inspector. Generate again, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
- Speaker colours apply only to the Subtitles style.
- Changing the number of words on a word caption page drops its word timing. To time it again, generate again.
- A style cannot be switched on a placed track. Restyle by generating again with Replace.

## For agents

| Tool | Mirrors |
|---|---|
| `import_captions` | File ▸ Import Captions… |
| `transcribe` | File ▸ Generate Captions… |
| `export_captions` | File ▸ Export Captions… |
| `get_transcript` | Reads one clip's words with their timeline times, from the cached transcript or this Mac's recogniser. It never uses the network and edits nothing. Used for cutting by transcript ([Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)). |

In the built-in [Assistant](assistant.md), `transcribe` with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld, because audio leaves the Mac only when a person chooses that in the sheet. `export_captions` asks before it writes a file. The full reference is [MCP](mcp.md).

Filler-word removal, which needs an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words, is covered in [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md). The Settings window as a whole is covered in [Settings](settings.md).

content.content:
An adjustment clip has no Picture tab, because it has no picture of its own
(see [Color grading](color-grading.md)).

Picture's sections, in order:

| Section | Shown for |
|---|---|
| Transform | every clip that draws |
| Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key | video, image and still clips |
| Shadow, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight, Obscure | every clip that draws, text and shapes included |

Each section folds open and shut and shows a one-line summary while closed.
Transform starts open. **Reset** appears only while a section differs from its
default. With several clips selected, a field shows the first clip's value and
a mixed badge when the others differ. An edit applies to every selected clip.
Colour swatches open the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.

*Agents:* `set_video` (merges a patch into each clip's video properties: `x`,
`y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend`, `crop`, `corner_radius`,
`shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure`).

### Transform

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Scale | 1–1000 % (quick values 25–400) | 100 % |
| Position X / Y | −20000 to 20000 canvas px, measured from the canvas centre, X right and Y down | 0, 0 |
| Rotation | −180° to 180° | 0° |
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 100 % |
| Blend | the eight blend modes below | Normal |

Two buttons sit under the rows:

- **Fit to Canvas** scales each clip so its whole picture fits, and centres it.
- **Fill Canvas** scales each clip until it covers the whole canvas, and
  centres it.

Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. Reset
Transform sets position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend back to their
defaults.

#### Blend modes

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| Normal | Draws over what is underneath |
| Multiply | Darkens by multiplying with what is underneath |
| Screen | Lightens, the inverse of multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow |
| Add | Adds the colours together |
| Overlay | Multiplies the darks and screens the lights |
| Darken | Keeps the darker of the two colours |
| Lighten | Keeps the lighter of the two colours |
| Difference | The absolute difference of the two colours |

A blend needs something under the layer. Over the empty black canvas,
Multiply, Darken and Overlay read black, and Screen, Add, Lighten and
Difference change nothing. When that is what is happening, the section says
so, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." The
note looks at the clip's whole span, not just the playhead. It ignores hidden
tracks and clips with their video turned off, and it appears only while the
canvas background is opaque black. To get a layer to blend against, use
**Clip ▸ Add Background** (see [Backgrounds](#backgrounds)), or set a
non-black canvas background on the Document tab. The Blend popup's tooltip
gives the same explanation.

Limits:

- A cross dissolve draws as Normal for as long as the clips overlap.
- The Blend popup is greyed on a nest clip, because a nest has no pixels of its
  own to blend. Un-nest it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside.
- Blend is an ordinary property, so an action can change it. Like any
  on/off-style value, the change happens at the action's end.

### Corner Radius

Radius: 0–500 px in source pixels (quick values 0–64). It rounds the cropped
picture's corners. Default 0.

### Chroma Key

Chroma Key removes a background colour, such as a green screen.

| Row | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Key out a color | Turns the key on | off |
| Key Color | The colour to remove | pure green |
| Pick from Canvas | Arms an eyedropper ("Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel"). One click on the preview sets the key colour and turns the key on. A second press of the button, Esc or a change of selection cancels it | — |
| Tolerance | How far from the key colour still counts as background, 0–100 % | 20 % |
| Softness | How gradual the edge of the key is, 0–100 % | 10 % |
| Spill | How much of the key colour's spill is removed from the edges that remain, 0–100 % | 50 % |

### Shadow

A drop shadow cast by the layer's own shape: the picture, the letters of a
text clip, or a shape's outline and fill.

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Drop shadow | on / off | off |
| Color | any | black |
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 50 % |
| Blur | 0–200 px | 12 px |
| Angle | 0–360° | 315° |
| Distance | 0–200 px | 8 px |

### Filters

A clip can carry up to **four** filters. They are applied in list order, so
blur-then-sepia looks different from sepia-then-blur.

- **Add Filter** appends a Blur at 50 %.
- Each filter's row starts with a number popup that is its place in the
  stack. Pick a different number to move the filter.
- The kind popup has **Blur**, **Sharpen**, **Pixelate**, **Sepia**, **Noir**,
  **Vignette** and **Invert**.
- **Amount** is 0–100 %.
- **Remove** takes a filter off.

An action can animate a filter's amount, for example a blur that ramps up
across a clip. Adding or removing a filter always changes the clip itself,
even while an action is selected.

### Reflection

**Mirror the layer below itself** hangs a mirrored copy under the layer. The
reflection rotates with the layer, and the layer always draws over its own
reflection.

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Opacity | 0–100 % | 35 % |
| Height | 0–100 % of the layer's height | 50 % |
| Gap | 0–200 px | 0 px |
| Falloff | 0–100 % | 100 % |

### Spotlight

**Spotlight a region** dims the canvas outside a rectangle or ellipse on the
clip, and can magnify what is inside.

| Row | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | Rectangle, Ellipse | Rectangle |
| Center X / Y | px from the centre of the clip's picture | 0, 0 |
| Width / Height | 1–20000 px | 480 × 270 |
| Feather | 0–200 px | 40 px |
| Dim | 0–100 % | 60 % |
| Zoom | 1.00–2.00× | 1.00× |

The spotlight's centre and size are measured in the clip's own source pixels.
The spotlight therefore stays on the same part of the picture when you move,
scale or rotate the clip.

### Obscure

Obscure hides a face, a password field or a phone number behind up to **four**
blurred or pixelated regions per clip.

- **Add Region** adds a 480 × 270 pixelated box at the centre of the layer.
- **Place on Canvas** arms a drawing mode ("Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc
  to cancel"). Drag a rectangle over the selected clip to add a region there.
  A drag smaller than 6 px is treated as a miss, and the mode stays armed. The
  mode needs exactly one selected clip that is drawing at the playhead and has
  a free slot. Esc, a second press of the button, or a change of selection
  ends the mode, and so does the playhead leaving the clip.
- Only one canvas mode can be armed at a time: Place on Canvas, Zoom to
  Region (**Z**, see [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)),
  Chroma Key's Pick from Canvas, and the qualifier's Pick from Canvas (see
  [Color grading](color-grading.md)). Arming one ends whichever other was
  armed.
- Each **Region N** row has a kind popup, **Pixelate** (hides) or **Blur**
  (softens), and a **Remove** button. Under it are **Shape** (Rectangle,
  Ellipse), **Amount** (0–100 %, default 100 %), **Feather** (0–200 px,
  default 20 px), **Center** (x, y) and **Size** (width, height, at least
  1 px).

On the canvas, the selected clip's regions are drawn as dashed outlines.
Drag a region's centre cross to move it. Drag one of its eight handles to
resize it, holding ⌥ to resize about its centre. The clip's own handles win
where they overlap a region, and a drag inside a region moves the clip. Esc
cancels the drag.

Regions are stored in the clip's own source pixels, so they follow the layer
through every move, scale, rotation and crop. Each region's numbers can be
animated like any other property. **Add Region**, **Place on Canvas** and
**Remove** always change the clip itself, not the selected action.

## Text clips

Press **T**, or use the timeline bar's **Add Text** button, to add a text clip
at the playhead. It goes on the front-most track if there is room, or on a new
track in front of everything if there isn't. The new clip:

- reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, white, centred
- lasts 5 seconds
- is selected, so the **Text** sub-tab opens on it

A text clip has no source file, so you can trim it to any length.
Double-click it on the canvas to type (see
[Inline text editing](#inline-text-editing)).

*Agents:* `add_text_clip` (track, at, optional duration and text, either a
plain string or a text patch); `set_text` to restyle.

### The Text tab

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Content** | A multi-line text area. Return, Tab or a click away applies it and gives the keys back to the editor; ⇧Return, ⌘Return, ⌥Return or ⌃Return starts a new line |
| **Font** | **Family** (every font installed on the Mac, plus the faces the app ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono), **Style** (that family's faces), **Size** 6–800 px |
| **Style** | **Color**, **Align** (L / C / R), **Vertical** (top / middle / bottom within the box), **UPPERCASE**, **Line spacing** 0.5–4× (default 1), **Tracking** −20 to 100 px (default 0) |
| **Outline** | **Outline** on/off, **Width** 0–40 px (default 2), **Color** (default black) |
| **Backdrop** | A plate behind the text: **Backdrop** on/off, **Fill** (default black at 60 %), **Padding** 0–200 px (default 12), **Radius** 0–200 px (default 8) |
| **Box** | **Mode**: **Auto-size** (the box fits the words) or **Fixed width** (the words wrap). **Width** is 20–20000 px, starting at 60 % of the canvas width |
| **Reveal** | How the text arrives and leaves: **None**, **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise**, with separate **In** and **Out** durations (0–10 s; In defaults to 1 s and Out to 0) measured from the clip's first and last frame |
| **Presets** | One-click looks, described below |

UPPERCASE changes only how the text is drawn: what you typed is kept as typed.
A text clip also gets the Picture tab's Transform, Shadow, Filters,
Reflection, Spotlight and Obscure sections.

Every frame of a reveal is worked out by the same calculation for the
preview, a rendered frame and an export, so the three always agree. A text
clip made by word captions has a word style, and while it does, the Reveal
section is greyed with "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply." (see
[Captions](captions.md)).

### Text presets

Each preset sets the face, size, alignment, backdrop and position in one
undo step. It also sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %.
Sizes and positions are fractions of the canvas, so a preset fits any canvas
size. With an action selected on the action lane, a preset sets that
action's end state, like any other field.

| Preset | Face | Size (of canvas height) | Placement | Backdrop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Title | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | centred | none |
| Subtitle | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | centred, 18 % of the height below centre | none |
| Lower Third | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | left-aligned, left of centre and low | black at 55 %, padding 18, radius 6 |
| Caption | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | centred, near the bottom | black at 60 %, padding 12, radius 8 |

## Shape clips

Click the timeline bar's **Add Shape** button and pick **Rectangle**,
**Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**. Like text, the shape goes on the front-most
track if there is room, lasts 5 seconds, can be trimmed to any length, and
opens on the **Shape** sub-tab.

A new shape is a 320 × 120 box with a 6 px white stroke and no fill, so it
shows up over any footage. A new arrow has its head at the end turned on. A
new line or arrow runs diagonally across its box. A rounded rectangle is a
Rectangle with a corner radius, not a separate kind.

*Agents:* `add_shape_clip` (track, at, optional duration and shape, either a
kind name or a shape patch); `set_shape` for geometry and paint.

### The Shape tab

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| **Shape** | **Kind** (Rectangle, Ellipse, Line, Arrow), **Width** and **Height** 1–20000 px, **Corner radius** 0–2000 px (rectangles only) |
| **Stroke** | **Stroke** on/off, **Width** 0.5–200 px (default 6), **Color** (default white) |
| **Fill** | **Fill** on/off (white when first turned on), **Color**, **Opacity** 0–100 % |
| **Gradient** | Fills the shape with a colour ramp in place of the flat fill (below) |
| **Arrowheads** | **Arrowhead at start**, **Arrowhead at end** (lines and arrows only) |

A shape also gets the Picture tab's Transform, Shadow, Filters, Reflection,
Spotlight and Obscure sections.

### Gradients

Tick **Gradient** to fill a rectangle or ellipse with a colour ramp. A new
gradient is **Linear**, black to white, at 0°.

- **Kind**: **Linear** or **Radial**.
- **Angle**: 0–360°, linear only. 0° runs to the right and the angle turns
  counter-clockwise.
- **Stop N** rows: a colour swatch, a position (0–100 % along the ramp) and
  **Remove**. A gradient keeps at least two stops.
- **Add Stop** puts a new stop in the middle of the widest gap, in the colour
  the ramp already has there. A gradient can have up to **eight** stops.

Past the first and last stops, the end colours continue to the shape's edge.
While a gradient is on it covers the Fill colour, and the section says so.
Reset turns the gradient off and brings the flat fill back. Lines and arrows
have no area to fill: the Gradient section is greyed for them and they keep
their stroke colour.

### Animated colours

When an action changes a colour (the text colour, its outline or backdrop, a
word-caption colour, the drop shadow or the chroma key colour), the colour
blends through the OKLab colour space. This avoids the muddy midpoint a
straight RGB blend gives. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

Shape colours (stroke, fill and gradient stops) cannot be animated: a
shape's styling always changes the clip itself, even while an action is
selected.

## Image clips

You import an image the same way as a movie (see
[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)), and it lands as a 5-second clip.
An image has no length of its own, so you can trim it to any duration. Image
clips have everything on the Picture tab, Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key
included, and a Color tab for grading.

When the Document tab's **Fit new clips to canvas** option is on, a new clip whose picture
is bigger than the canvas starts at Fit scale. Otherwise it starts at 100 %,
its native size.

## Backgrounds

Backgrounds are in the Clip menu. Each command puts a clip on a **new
back-most track** and selects it.

| Command | What it puts there |
|---|---|
| **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color** | A canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. White because the canvas is already black. Recolour it in the Shape tab's Fill row, or turn on Gradient for a full-canvas ramp |
| **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…** | A picture you choose (the panel offers only image files), scaled to fill the canvas, as long as the timeline. The picture joins the Media tab in the same undo step, or is reused if it is already there. If it can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added |
| **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** | A copy of the one selected clip, playing exactly the same frames, scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped and blurred at full strength. It is muted so the sound doesn't play twice, and is named "Blurred Background". This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video that doesn't fill the frame |

Limits:

- Add Blurred Background needs exactly one selected clip. It is dimmed for a
  text clip, an adjustment clip, an audio-only clip and a nest clip, none of
  which has a picture size to scale to the canvas. Video, image, still, shape
  and graphic clips can all take one.
- The blurred copy takes no transition, actions, label or ducking from the
  original.
- When an agent places a video plate, the plate stops where its file ends.

*Agents:* `add_background` (optional `color`, `media` or `duration`; with no
arguments it adds the white plate); `add_blurred_background` (`clip`).

## Matte tracks

A matte track cuts the track directly behind it. Its own clips are never
drawn. Instead, what they show decides where the track behind can be seen. Any
clip that draws can be a matte: text, a shape, a graphic, an image, a movie or
a nest. That makes it a window onto the footage beneath, in the preview,
rendered frames and every export.

Set the mode with **Track ▸ Matte**, or with the **Matte** submenu of a
track's context menu (right-click its header):

| Mode | The track behind shows where the matte clip is… |
|---|---|
| **Off** | (an ordinary track) |
| **Alpha** | opaque |
| **Inverted Alpha** | transparent |
| **Luma** | bright |
| **Inverted Luma** | dark |

How a matte behaves:

- Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut.
- Hiding the matte track, or turning off a matte clip's video, turns the cut
  off, and the track behind shows whole.
- A matte with no target cuts nothing and still draws nothing. That happens
  for a matte on the back-most track, or one directly in front of another
  matte track.
- A matte clip's position, scale, rotation, crop, opacity, colour, filters,
  actions and transitions all shape the matte, so a moving title can wipe
  footage on.
- A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect. The
  values are kept, and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
- A matte clip's sound still plays.
- An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect.

When the selection sits on a matte track, every Clip sub-tab shows a note
under its sub-tab strip, and every control stays live:

| Selection | Note |
|---|---|
| Clips on a matte track with a track behind it | "Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect." (with the track's mode) |
| Clips on a matte track with nothing behind it | "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing." |
| Adjustment clips on a matte track | "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." |

### Mattes inside nests

A matte track works inside a nest just as it does on the timeline. A clip
inside a nest that sits on a matte track (directly, or because the nest clip
does) becomes a matte at the first matte track found going outward.

- **Nest** keeps a track's matte only when the track it cuts is nested with
  it. A matte nested without its target becomes an ordinary track inside the
  nest. The nest clip goes on the front-most of the nested clips' tracks
  that is not a matte track.
- **Un-nest** lines the nest's front-most non-matte track up with the nest
  clip's track, so the picture comes back as it was.

See [Editing](editing.md) for nesting itself.

On the timeline, a matte track's header carries a tag such as "Matte · Alpha",
or a dimmed "Matte · nothing behind" when there is nothing to cut. Its clips
are drawn at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins it to the
track it cuts.

*Agents:* `set_track` (`matte`: `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or
`luma_inverted`).

## Copying a look between clips

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) puts the look of the clip you copied onto
every selected clip, in one undo step. The look is its picture settings, its
sound settings, and its text or shape styling. A text clip keeps its own words
and a shape keeps its kind and size. **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**
does the same for graphic clips. See [Editing](editing.md) for exactly what
is copied.

*Agents:* `paste_attributes`.

## Limits

- Scale is uniform for pictures. Only shapes (box width and height) and text
  (wrap width) can be stretched on one axis.
- At most four filters and four obscure regions per clip. Gradients have 2–8
  stops.
- Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key are only for video, image and still
  clips.
- A nest clip can't take a blend mode, and Add Blurred Background is not
  offered for one.
- Locked tracks can't be edited on the canvas, and hidden tracks can't be
  clicked there.
- The canvas text editor stays upright even for a rotated text clip. The text
  you apply is the same either way.

# Canvas, layers, text and shapes

The preview canvas is where you place a clip's picture. Select a layer on it,
then drag to move, scale, rotate or crop it. The Clip tab's **Picture**
sub-tab holds the same placement as numbers, along with opacity, blend modes,
shadows, filters and the effects that hide or highlight part of a frame. This
page also covers what you can put on the canvas besides footage: text clips,
shape clips, image clips, background plates, and matte tracks, which cut the
track behind them.

Every clip that draws can be edited the same way: video, image, still, text,
shape, graphic and nest. A track never holds just one kind of clip. Tracks
stack back to front, and a track higher in the timeline draws in front.

## The canvas

The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size,
centred in the preview pane. Under it is a small caption with the canvas size
and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`. You set the canvas size,
rate and background colour on the Document tab (see
[Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

### Zoom and pan

| Do this | To |
|---|---|
| Toolbar zoom popup: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Pick a zoom stop |
| **View ▸ Zoom In** (⌘+ or ⌘=), **View ▸ Zoom Out** (⌘-) | Step through the same four stops |
| **View ▸ Zoom to Fit** (⌘0) | Go back to Fit |
| Pinch on the trackpad, or ⌥-scroll / ⌘-scroll | Step through the stops |
| Hold Space and drag, or scroll | Pan, when the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane |

A Space tap that does not pan still plays and pauses as usual.

**View ▸ Preview Window** (⇧⌘P) opens a second window with the same picture
and no handles, for a second display.

### Selecting

- Click a layer to select the topmost visible clip under the pointer at the
  playhead. Hit-testing follows the layer's rotation.
- ⇧-click adds a clip to the selection or removes it.
- Click empty canvas to clear the selection.
- Clips on hidden tracks are not drawn, so you can't click them. Clips on
  locked tracks are drawn but can't be selected or moved on the canvas.
- A clip on a matte track can be selected and dragged like any other clip
  inside its own box, even though it draws nothing there (see
  [Matte tracks](#matte-tracks)). Because it is topmost inside that box, a
  click there selects the matte clip. To select the clip it cuts, click
  outside the matte clip's box, or use the timeline.

The selected clips get an outline. The front-most selected clip also gets
handles.

### Move, scale and rotate

| Gesture | What it does |
|---|---|
| Drag inside the box | Move. Every selected clip moves by the same amount |
| ← → ↑ ↓ (canvas focused) | Nudge the selection 1 canvas pixel |
| ⇧ + arrow | Nudge 10 pixels |
| Drag one of the eight square handles | Scale (see below) |
| ⌥ while scaling | Scale about the centre instead of pinning the opposite handle |
| Drag the round grip above the top edge | Rotate about the clip's centre |
| ⇧ while rotating | Snap the angle to 15° steps |
| Esc during any drag | Cancel the drag and put the clip back where it was, with no undo step |

How a scale drag behaves depends on the clip:

- **Video, image, still, graphic and nest clips** have one uniform scale. Every
  handle scales the whole picture and keeps its aspect ratio.
- **Shape clips** change their box size instead. A corner handle keeps the
  aspect ratio and ⇧ frees it. An edge handle changes only the width or only
  the height.
- **Text clips**: the left and right edge handles set the text box's wrap
  width, which makes the box fixed-width. The corners and the top and bottom
  edges scale the text uniformly.

A drag scales between 1 % and 1000 %. Each drag is one undo step, and a click
that doesn't move anything adds no step.

There is no separate anchor-point control. Rotation, the Picture tab's Scale
field and a ⌥ scale drag pivot on the centre of the clip's uncropped picture.
A plain handle drag keeps the opposite handle in place by moving the clip as
it scales.

### Line and arrow endpoints

A line or arrow shape has a round handle at each end. Drag a handle to move
that end. The scale handles and the rotation grip still work on the line's
box.

### Snapping

While you drag a clip to move it, the box snaps to:

- the canvas edges, its centre lines and its thirds
- the edges and centres of every other visible layer

Scaling, rotating and cropping do not snap (⇧ while rotating snaps the angle
to 15° steps instead). A guide line is drawn across the canvas on each axis that snapped. Press
**N** or choose **View ▸ Snapping** to turn snapping on or off. The timeline
uses the same setting. Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for that drag.

### Safe areas

**View ▸ Safe Areas**, or the toolbar's **Safe** checkbox, draws two guide
frames over the canvas, at 90 % and 80 % of its size. They are guides only
and never appear in an export. The app remembers the setting.

### Editing an action's end state on the canvas

With an action selected on the clip's action lane, a move, scale, rotate or
crop drag, or an arrow-key nudge, edits that action's end state, just as the
inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the
playhead. There are two exceptions: a drag on a multi-clip selection, and a
shape's box resize, both edit the clip itself. See
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## Crop

Press **C**, or double-click a clip that is not text, to enter crop mode for
the selected clip. The eight handles become crop edges, and the part being
cut away is shown as a dim ghost inside the uncropped frame. Press **Esc** or
**Return**, or click empty canvas, to leave crop mode.

A crop removes edges in place: the picture never shifts as you crop. Crop
amounts are in the source's own pixels, so they stay correct when you scale
the clip later. The core keeps at least one source pixel in each direction.

The Picture tab's **Crop** section has the same four insets as fields, plus a
**Crop on Canvas** button that enters crop mode. Crop appears only for clips
with pixels of their own, which means video, image and still clips.

## Inline text editing

Double-click a text clip on the canvas to type into it in place. The editor
uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, and
it grows and wraps as you type, the way the text will once you apply it.
UPPERCASE text is edited as you typed it.

| Key | In the canvas text editor |
|---|---|
| Return (or keypad Enter) | Apply the text and close the editor |
| ⇧Return, ⌥Return, ⌘Return or ⌃Return | New line |
| Esc | Close at once if nothing changed. Otherwise a sheet asks **Apply** (the default), **Revert** or **Cancel** |
| Click elsewhere | Apply |

While an input method is composing, Return and Esc go to the input method.

## The Picture tab

Select a clip and open the inspector's **Clip** tab. Its sub-tabs depend on
what is selected:

- Text clips start on **Text** and shapes on **Shape**.
- Any clip that draws has **Picture**.
- **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip** follow where they apply.

An adjustment clip has no Picture tab, because it has no picture of its own

content.content:
# Motion, actions and transitions

Frame Job has three ways to make a clip move or change over time. An **action** animates a clip's properties from one state to another over a span you choose: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. **Motion presets** give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that stays tied to the clip's two ends. A **transition** plays where two clips on one track overlap. This page covers all three, and what the Clip tab shows while you work on an action.

## Actions

An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties ease from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve. When the span is over, the clip holds the end state until a later action changes it again.

- An action's times are measured from the clip's own start (clip time), not from the start of the timeline.
- Actions on one clip may not overlap. A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end.
- Several actions run in time order. Each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.
- A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it.

### How values change over an action

| Kind of value | What happens over the span |
|---|---|
| Numbers (position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders, a graphic's number properties) | Ramp along the action's curve |
| Colours (shadow, chroma key, text colours, word-caption colours, a graphic's colour properties) | Ramp in OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact |
| Switches, popups and text (an on/off box, a filter's kind, a font, a graphic's string, boolean or image property) | Hold, then switch to the end value when the action ends |
| Lists (filters, obscure regions) | Ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries. If the list's length changes, the whole list switches at the end. If one entry changes kind (or a region its shape), only that entry switches at the end and the others still ramp |
| Curves | Always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point; a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points; two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action |

The four curves are the same everywhere an action or a transition is eased:

| Curve | Lane label | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| Linear | Linear | Constant speed |
| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast |
| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly |
| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends |

A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action is **Ease In Out**.

### What an action can animate

- **Picture.** Everything in the Picture sub-tab that is a value: transform, opacity, crop, corner radius, shadow, reflection, spotlight, the amounts inside filters and obscure regions. See [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md).
- **Color.** Light, Colour, Wheels, Curves, Look amount and, on an adjustment clip, Strength and the Qualifier. See [Color grading](color-grading.md).
- **Sound.** The Sound sub-tab's Volume and Fades sections. See [Audio](audio.md).
- **Text.** The Text sub-tab's style, size and colours. See [Captions](captions.md) for word captions.
- **Graphics.** A graphic clip's properties. Numbers and colours ramp; strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable cannot be put in an action. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Speed.** A media clip's playback rate, which makes a speed ramp. See [Speed](speed.md).

Some things are never animated. These rows write the clip itself, whatever is selected, and are marked ⊘ in the Clip tab:

- The Motion presets section (below).
- In the Sound sub-tab: Ducking, the fade shapes, the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's Mix to mono. Every other audio setting animates ([Audio](audio.md#animating-the-sound)).
- In the Clip sub-tab's Speed section: Keep pitch and Fit to.
- **Adding or removing** a filter or an obscure region. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
- A shape's own properties in the Shape sub-tab (its kind, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows). Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's.

### Add an action

1. Select a clip and put the playhead over it.
2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (⌥⌘K), or click **+** (Add Action) in the Clip tab's action lane.

The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and is selected straight away, so the Clip tab is ready to edit its end state.

- **Clip ▸ Add Action** is unavailable (greyed out) unless the playhead is over a selected clip. The action lane's **+** button beeps in that case.
- With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and is not selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** also makes actions: one for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst. They show as bands and edit like any other action. See [Speed](speed.md).

The action is refused when it would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end, so near the end of a clip move the playhead back first, or shorten an existing action.

*Agents:* `add_action` (clip, `at` in clip time, optional `duration`; answers the new id in `new_actions`).

### Zoom to a region

**Zoom to Region** is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms so that rectangle fills the frame.

1. Select one clip and put the playhead over it.
2. Press **Z**, or click the zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region) in the action lane.
3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. A hint reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel", and a second outline shows exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands.
4. Release the mouse.

Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas. It works through the clip's rotation and crop. The new action is selected.

- **Fit or fill.** By default the whole rectangle is shown (fit). Hold **⇧** while dragging to fill the canvas instead, cropping whatever doesn't match the canvas shape.
- **Scale limit.** The zoom stops at the largest scale a layer can take, and the rectangle stays centred even then.
- **Leaving the mode.** Press Esc, press **Z** again, or click the button again. The mode also closes when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip. A rectangle too small to mean anything beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.
- **During motion.** If the clip has a During motion preset, the band shows "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it", because the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom.

The mode needs exactly one selected clip that is drawn at the playhead and is not on a locked track. Otherwise **Z** beeps.

**Zoom Back** (the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane) adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own base scale, x and y, whatever earlier actions did. Use it after a Zoom to Region to pull back out. It needs the same target as **Z** (one selected clip drawn at the playhead, not on a locked track) and beeps otherwise. The new action is selected.

*Agents:* `add_zoom_action` (`region` as centre and size in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, `fit` or `fill`, optional `curve` and `duration`; `region: null` is a zoom back).

### Select an action

An action is selected when you:

- click its band in the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane,
- add it (with Add Action, Zoom to Region or Zoom Back), or
- play or scrub the playhead **into** its span while its clip is the only one selected.

Clicking a band on a clip that is part of a multi-clip selection selects just that clip and its action.

Clicking a band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state the Clip tab is editing (one frame short when the action ends with the clip).

Leaving the span keeps the action selected. To leave it, press **Esc**, click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane, or select a different clip. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Selecting an action is not an undo step and is not saved with the project.

### Edit an action's end state

While an action is selected, every field in the Clip tab shows and sets that action's **end state**, the values the clip reaches at the action's end. The same goes for the canvas: dragging the selected clip's handles, or nudging it with the arrow keys, writes the end state.

Unchecking a switch inside an action (a shadow or an outline, for example) turns that property off when the action ends.

The Clip tab marks each row so you can see what the action touches:

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ◆ | This action animates the row. The label turns strong and the field gets a border in the action colour. A popup, checkbox or other on/off control also shows "at end", because it switches rather than ramps |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates this row. Its tooltip names the action |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates (for example, Gain follows Volume) |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row. Edits change the clip |

A slider on an animated row fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. When the playhead is inside the clip, a coral tick shows the value at the playhead. A row that is a field only shows that value as a "now …" tag instead.

Section headers carry the same marks, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N of its keys. When you select an action, the sections it animates on the current sub-tab open automatically.

To take a property back out of an action:

- Hover over a ◆ and click the × that replaces it ("Remove from action N").
- Click **Clear** in a section's header to remove all of that section's keys from the action. While an action is selected and keys the section, Clear takes the place of the header's **Reset**; otherwise Reset shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
- Right-click a row for its menu: **Remove from action N** on an animated row, **Go to action M** on a ◇ row (selects that action), and **Set end value to default** (on a row the selected action animates) or **Reset to default** (otherwise). The default item is disabled when the row already holds its default.

*Agents:* `set_action_end` (a `patch` with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`, merged into the end state; `null` removes a key; `off` lists `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end). `video.motion` and `text.words` are refused.

### Move, resize and re-curve an action
....

## Motion presets

A motion preset says what a clip **does** rather than where it is. Each clip has three slots: an **In** (an entrance at its start), an **Out** (an exit at its end) and a **During** (a movement for its whole length). A preset is tied to the clip's ends, so it moves with a trim. It works on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

Motion is applied on top of the clip's own placement and any actions, and it is never animated by an action. A preset works relative to the clip: its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own, and its rotation and offset add to them. Zoom and Spin turn about the clip's visible centre, after any crop. The inspector fields (and `get_project`) show the clip's own, un-moved values, even though the preview and export show it moving.

### Set a preset

Use the **Motion presets** section at the end of the Clip sub-tab, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In**, **Out** or **During**. Each submenu lists the kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares.

The section's rows:

| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| In | The entrance kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| In Duration | How long the entrance takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| Out | The exit kind, or None | None and nine kinds | None |
| Out Duration | How long the exit takes (disabled with None) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1) | 0.5 s |
| During | The continuous movement, or None | None and five kinds | None |
| Amount | How strong the During movement is (disabled with None) | 0–100% (quick picks 25, 50, 75, 100) | 50% |
| Period | How long one cycle takes (disabled with None and for Drift) | 0.1–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) | 1 s |
| Preview | Sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and plays it | | |

Changing a slot's kind keeps the duration, amount and period it already had. The section is closed by default, and its summary reads, for example, "in fade · out slide left · pulse", or "off". **Reset** clears all three slots. With several clips selected, each one keeps its own other slots. Preview leaves the range and Loop on until you clear them.

**Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview** does the same as the Preview button. With several clips selected, both loop the first selected clip that has a picture.

*Agents:* `set_video` with `motion: {in: {kind, duration}, out: {kind, duration}, during: {kind, amount, period}}` (durations and period in ticks, amount 0–1; `motion: null` clears all three).

### Entrances and exits

The same nine kinds fill both In and Out. An exit is the entrance played the other way: the In eases out as it arrives, and the Out eases in as it leaves.

| Kind | As an entrance (In) | As an exit (Out) |
|---|---|---|
| Fade | Fades in | Fades out |
| Zoom In | Grows from 60% to full size while fading in | Grows to 140% while fading out |
| Zoom Out | Shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in | Shrinks to 60% while fading out |
| Slide Left | Slides in from the right edge | Slides out past the left edge |
| Slide Right | Slides in from the left edge | Slides out past the right edge |
| Slide Up | Slides in from the bottom edge | Slides out past the top edge |
| Slide Down | Slides in from the top edge | Slides out past the bottom edge |
| Spin | Spins half a turn into place from 30% size, fading in | Spins half a turn away to 30% size, fading out |
| Pop | Springs up past full size (to about 110%) and settles, fading in over the first quarter | Swells and springs away, fading out over the last quarter |

A slide measures the layer as it is drawn, so it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas (or of the nest it is inside).

### During

| Kind | What it does |
|---|---|
| Pulse | Gently grows and shrinks once per period, up to 20% larger at 100% |
| Shake | Jitters in a pattern that never visibly repeats, up to 4% of the canvas's shorter edge at 100% |
| Spin | Rotates continuously; at 50%, one full turn per period |
| Bounce | Hops upward once per period, up to 8% of the canvas height at 100% |
| Drift | A slow push-in across the whole clip, ending up to 24% larger at 100%. It ignores Period |

Every During movement starts from the clip's own placement on its first frame. It runs under the In and Out, so a clip can, for example, slide in while it pulses.

### On the timeline

A clip with an In or Out preset shows a small wedge along the bottom of its name strip, as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom. If the wedges overlap, the two presets are longer than the clip together. In that case Frame Job shortens both in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins, rather than refusing.

A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip.

### Inactive presets

An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent or an older project. It is kept but does nothing. The section, the summary and the Motion menu mark it "(inactive)" (or "(some inactive)" across a selection), it draws no wedge, and a note reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."

### Limits

- A preset is not part of any action. Motion rows are ⊘, and edits always write the clip, even with an action selected.
- A split gives the first half no Out and the second half no In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. A During movement restarts at each cut, so Remove Silences on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
- Freeze frame and Add Blurred Background drop the motion. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it. Changing the speed doesn't rescale the presets.
- A text clip has no measured size, so a slide starts or ends half a canvas past the edge. That clears any text narrower than the canvas.
- A canvas drag started mid-motion starts from the clip's un-moved position.

## Transitions

A transition plays across the **overlap** between two clips on the same track. The overlap's length is the transition's duration, and the later clip carries the transition (it is the transition *into* that clip). The overlap is drawn on the timeline as a hatched zone, with the transition's name in it when the word fits.

Two rules limit overlaps: a clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and an overlap can be at most half as long as the shorter of the two clips. Clips never push each other out of the way. A move that would break either rule is refused.

### Transition styles

| Style | What it does |
|---|---|
| Cross Dissolve | The outgoing clip fades into the incoming one |
| Fade Through Black | The outgoing clip fades to black over the first half, then the incoming one fades up from black over the second half |
| Fade Through White | The same, through white (in an HLG project, the lifted SDR white) |
| Push Left | Both clips move: the outgoing leaves to the left as the incoming pushes in from the right |
| Push Right | The outgoing leaves to the right, the incoming comes in from the left |
| Push Up | The outgoing leaves upward, the incoming comes up from the bottom |
| Push Down | The outgoing leaves downward, the incoming comes down from the top |
| Wipe | An edge sweeps left to right, revealing the incoming clip |
| Wipe Left | An edge sweeps right to left |
| Wipe Up | An edge sweeps upward |
| Wipe Down | An edge sweeps downward |
| Slide | The incoming clip slides in from the right over the outgoing one, which stays put |
| Zoom | The outgoing clip grows toward you (to 125%) while the incoming one grows into place from 75%, and the two dissolve into each other |

A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line.

A fade through a colour changes the layer's own pixels toward the colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas (a picture-in-picture), the fade shows a black (or white) box over what is behind it, not a see-through fade.

### Add a transition

There are three ways:

- **Overlap two clips.** Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve, eased (Ease In Out) and crossfading the sound. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, insert, close a gap or shift clips.
- **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ \<style\>.** Works on every selected clip at once:
  - A clip that already overlaps the clip before it gets the chosen style, keeping its curve and crossfade.
  - A clip at a **hard cut** (it starts exactly where the previous clip ends) gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut. The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing: the source past the first clip's out point and before the second clip's in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were. If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter.
  - A clip after a gap, or the first clip on its track, is skipped.

  A style is enabled only when at least one selected clip is at an overlap or a hard cut. The checkmark shows the first selected clip's style, or None when it has no transition. None is enabled for any selection.
- **The Transition section's Kind popup**, for a clip that already overlaps (below).

**When there is no footage to spare.** Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. Clip ▸ Transition ▸ then shows a sheet: "There's no extra footage at this cut for a transition." Choosing **Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The project gets that much shorter, and no clip's footage changes. Markers don't move. A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve. The whole shift is one undo step. **Cancel** changes nothing.

*Agents:* `add_transition` (the hard-cut form: `kind`, `duration`, `align` `center`, `before` or `after`, and `ripple: true` for the Shift Clips Left form); `set_transition` (a kind onto a clip that already overlaps).

### The Transition section

The **Transition** section is on the Clip sub-tab when a single selected clip overlaps the clip before it. Its summary reads, for example, "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none".

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Kind | The style, or None | None and the thirteen styles |
| Curve | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |
| Crossfade Audio | On: the outgoing sound fades out and the incoming fades in, eased by the Curve, in the Crossfade Shape. A pair where only one clip has sound still fades that clip. Off: both clips play at their own level across the whole overlap, mixed together. Mute, solo, ducking and volume still apply on top | On or off |
| Crossfade Shape | The curve of the crossfade, enabled while Crossfade Audio is on. **+3 dB** (constant power, the default) holds the level steady between two unrelated takes. **Linear** is a straight-line pair, which dips 3 dB in the middle of unrelated takes but suits two parts of the same sound. **S-Curve** and **−3 dB** move more of the change to the middle or the end. The incoming clip follows the shape and the outgoing clip follows it in reverse | +3 dB, Linear, S-Curve, −3 dB |
| Duration | The length of the overlap. Changing it **moves** the later clip to match | 0.02–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |

A transition Frame Job makes is eased (Ease In Out) and crossfades its sound. An overlap with no stored transition draws as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and in that state the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Setting either of them then stores a transition with exactly the values shown.

The duration is refused on a track's first clip, and past half the shorter clip. The refusal names the limit.

Two overlapping clips with no picture (audio-only clips) get the same section. Only their sound changes: Crossfade Audio and Curve control the crossfade, and Kind has no visible effect.

*Agents:* `set_transition_style` (`curve`, `audio` and `audio_shape` — `plus_3db`, `linear`, `s_curve`, `minus_3db` — each kept when absent); `set_transition_duration`.

### Remove a transition

Choose **None** in the Kind popup, or **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**. None is always available, because a clip can hold a transition the timeline doesn't draw: one left behind when an overlap was dragged apart, for example.

None removes the stored transition but not the overlap. While two clips still overlap they keep blending as a plain linear dissolve, with no hatch on the timeline. To get a hard cut back, move or trim the clips so they no longer overlap.

*Agents:* `set_transition` with `kind: null`.

### Limits

- A transition only plays across an overlap on one track. A transition stored on a clip that overlaps nothing does nothing until there is an overlap.
- Adjustment clips can't take a transition.
- After **Detach Audio**, Crossfade Audio on the video clips' transition has no effect, because their own sound is switched off. To crossfade the sound, overlap the detached audio clips and give them a transition of their own.
- Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words never cut into a transition's overlap. See [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md).
- A layer always blends normally while it is in a transition, whatever blend mode it has.
