## Frame Job menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| About Frame Job | | The version and credits panel |
| Check for Updates… | | Asks whether a newer Frame Job has been published, and offers to install it. Only in the copy you download from GitHub; a build from source has no updater ([Settings](settings.md#updates)) |
| Settings… | ⌘, | Opens the Settings window ([Settings](settings.md)) |
| Hide Frame Job | ⌘H | Hides the app |
| Hide Others | ⌥⌘H | Hides every other app |
| Show All | | Shows hidden apps again |
| Quit Frame Job | ⌘Q | Quits |

## File menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| New Project | ⌘N | A new, empty project window |
| New Recording… | ⌥⌘N | Opens the recorder. While a recording runs, the item is called **Stop Recording** and stops it ([Screen recording](screen-recording.md)) |
| Pause Recording | | Pauses the running recording. It is called **Resume Recording** while paused, and is enabled only during a recording |
| Open… | ⌘O | Opens a project or a media file |
| Open Recent ▸ | | Recently opened documents, then **Clear Menu** |
| Close | ⌘W | Closes the window |
| Save | ⌘S | Saves the project |
| Duplicate | ⇧⌘S | Opens a copy of the project as a new, untitled document. Hold ⌥ and the item becomes **Save As…** (⌥⇧⌘S), which writes the project to a new package |
| Rename… | | Renames the project's package |
| Move To… | | Moves the project's package to another folder |
| Revert To ▸ | | Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package |
| Share | | The macOS Share menu for the project |
| Add Media… | ⇧⌘I | Imports files into the project's Media list ([Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)) |
| Import Captions… | | Reads a caption file onto a caption track ([Captions](captions.md)) |
| Generate Captions… | | Makes captions from speech |
| Export Captions… | | Writes a caption track out as a file |
| Consolidate Media… | | Copies the project's media into the project package |
| Add Font to Graphics… | | Adds a font that graphics can use ([Graphics](graphics.md)) |
| Add Image to Graphics… | | Adds a picture that graphics can use |
| Rename Graphic… | | Renames one of the project's graphics. Greyed when the project has no graphics, or while a nest is open |
| Delete Graphic… | | Deletes a graphic that no clip uses |
| Restore Graphic Version… | | Brings back an earlier version of a graphic |
| Export… | ⌘E | The export sheet ([Export](export.md)) |
| Save Frame… | ⌥⌘E | Saves the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC still |

*Agents:* `new_project`, `open_project`, `save_project`, `close_project`,
`import_media`, `import_captions`, `transcribe`, `export_captions`,
`consolidate_media`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`,
`rename_graphic`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `export`,
`render_frame` (Save Frame…'s writer) and `record_screen`.

### When File items are available

| Item | Enabled when |
|---|---|
| Generate Captions… | Some clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on |
| Export Captions… | The project has a caption track: a track whose clips are all text clips |
| Consolidate Media… | The project has media |
| Rename Graphic… | The project has graphics and no nest is open |
| Delete Graphic… | The project has graphics |
| Restore Graphic Version… | An earlier version of a graphic is kept |
| Export…, Save Frame… | The project is not empty |

## Edit menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Undo | ⌘Z | Undoes the last edit. The item names it, for example **Undo Move Clips** or **Undo Ripple Delete** |
| Redo | ⇧⌘Z | Redoes it, named the same way |
| Cut | ⌘X | Cuts the selected clips |
| Copy | ⌘C | Copies the selected clips |
| Paste | ⌘V | Pastes clips at the playhead. Nothing needs to be selected |
| Paste Attributes | ⌥⌘V | Puts the copied clip's look onto the selected clips |
| Paste Graphic Properties | | Puts the copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips that use the same graphic |
| Duplicate | ⌘D | Copies the selected clips and places the copies after them |
| Delete | ⌫ | Removes the selection and leaves a gap. With nothing selected it lifts the in/out range. With an action selected it removes that action |
| Ripple Delete | ⌘⌫ | Removes the selection, or the in/out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap |
| Insert at Playhead | | Inserts the file selected in the Media tab, pushing later clips along |
| Overwrite at Playhead | | Places that file over whatever is already there |
| Select All | ⌘A | Selects every clip |
| Select After Playhead | ⌥⌘A | Selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead |
| Select All on Track | | Selects every clip on the current track |

Cut and Copy need a selection. Paste needs copied clips on the clipboard.
Paste Attributes needs copied clips and a selection. Paste Graphic
Properties needs copied clips and a selected graphic clip. Insert and
Overwrite at Playhead are enabled only while a file is selected in the Media
tab, and never for a LUT. Select All on Track needs a current track and a
timeline with clips. The *current track* is the track of the
first selected clip. With nothing selected it is the front-most track. See
[Editing](editing.md).

*Agents:* `undo`, `redo`, `paste`, `paste_attributes`, `duplicate`, `delete`,
`lift_range`, `ripple_delete`, `ripple_delete_range`, `insert_clip`,
`overwrite_clip`, `set_selection`.

## Insert menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Adjustment Clip | | Adds an adjustment clip over the in/out range. Without a range it covers the selected clips' span, and without a selection the whole timeline. Greyed while a nest is open ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Graphic… | | Opens the Graphic dialog: the bundled templates by category (and This Project's own graphics), a looping preview, and Insert to add the chosen one at the playhead, From File… to add a `.js` file or import a `.fjgraphic` you choose, or Export… to save the chosen one as a `.fjgraphic` file ([Graphics](graphics.md#adding-a-graphic)) |

*Agents:* `add_adjustment_clip`; `list_graphics` and `insert_graphic`, or
`write_graphic` followed by `add_graphic_clip`.

## Clip menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Split | ⌘T | Cuts the selected clips at the playhead. With nothing selected, it cuts every clip under the playhead |
| Trim Start to Playhead | W (key) | Trims the selected clips' starts to the playhead |
| Trim End to Playhead | E (key) | Trims their ends to the playhead |
| Freeze Frame | ⇧⌘F | Holds the frame under the playhead as a still clip |
| Detach Audio | ⌥⌘D | Moves a clip's sound onto its own clip, linked to it ([Audio](audio.md)) |
| Attach Audio | ⇧⌥⌘D | Merges a detached sound back into its picture ([Audio](audio.md#attach-audio)) |
| Normalize | | Sets the selected clips' volume to a loudness (the default, turning a clip's limiter on when its peaks need it) or a peak, by the mode chosen in the Volume section's Normalize row. A clip with processing is measured through it under the Measuring Sound sheet |
| Enhance Voice | | Sets the selected clips up for speech from their own measurements: high-pass, isolation or noise reduction and a gate for noisy pauses, the leveller for an uneven voice, the de-esser, a compressor, the limiter and the volume to the Normalize row's target ([Audio](audio.md#enhance-voice)) |
| Match Audio… | | Gives the selected clips the loudness and the speech's tone of one of them, chosen in a sheet: their volume and limiter, and their EQ's shelves and bands, measured under the Measuring Sound sheet ([Audio](audio.md#match-audio)) |
| Synchronize Audio | | Lines up the selected clips by their sound. Needs two or more clips that play sound |
| Add Action | ⌥⌘K | Adds an action at the playhead ([Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)) |
| Speed… | | Sets the selected clips' playback rate ([Speed](speed.md)) |
| Speed Ramp… | | Puts a speed ramp preset on one selected media clip |
| Close Gap | | Closes the gap under the playhead on the current track |
| Remove Silences… | | Finds silent stretches and removes them ([Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)) |
| Remove Filler Words… | | Finds "um"s and "uh"s and removes them |
| Transition ▸ | | Sets the transition into the clip |
| Motion ▸ | | Sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves |
| Look ▸ | | Puts a look or a LUT on the clip ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Add Background ▸ Solid Color | | Puts a colour plate on a new track behind everything ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)) |
| Add Background ▸ Image… | | Puts a picture you choose on a new track behind everything |
| Add Blurred Background | | Puts a blurred copy of the picture on a new track behind everything |
| Rename… | ⇧⌘R | Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline |
| Label ▸ | | Gives the clip a colour label |
| Nest | ⌘G | Wraps the selected clips into one nest clip |
| Un-nest | ⇧⌘G | Breaks a nest clip back into its clips |
| Open Nest | ⌘↓ | Goes inside the selected nest clip |
| Close Nest | ⌘↑ | Comes back out by one level |

### Clip submenus

- **Transition ▸**: Cross Dissolve, Fade Through Black, Fade Through White,
  Push Left, Push Right, Push Up, Push Down, Wipe, Slide, Zoom, Wipe Left,
  Wipe Up, Wipe Down, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's
  transition. A transition can be picked only on a clip that has room for
  one. **None** works for any selection, so a stored transition can always
  be cleared.
- **Motion ▸ In ▸** and **Motion ▸ Out ▸**: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide
  Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin, Pop, then **None**.
- **Motion ▸ During ▸**: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce, Drift, then **None**.
- In each Motion submenu a checkmark shows the kind every selected clip
  has. An In or Out kind whose length is zero reads **\<Kind\> (inactive)**,
  or **(some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind
  have zero length.
- **Motion ▸ Preview**: sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and
  plays it. The range and Loop stay set afterwards.
- **Look ▸**: Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic,
  Black & White. Then come the project's `.cube` LUTs, when it has any, and
  then **None**. A checkmark marks a look that every selected clip has. A
  dash marks one that only some of them have.
- **Label ▸**: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple (each shown with its
  colour dot), then **None**. A checkmark shows the label the selected clips
  share.

### When Clip items are available

| Item | Enabled when |
|---|---|
| Split | The timeline has any clip |
| Trim Start / End to Playhead, Freeze Frame | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| Detach Audio | Something is selected |
| Attach Audio | A selected clip is linked to its detached sound or picture |
| Normalize | A selected clip plays sound |
| Enhance Voice | A selected clip plays sound |
| Match Audio… | Two or more selected clips play sound |
| Synchronize Audio | Two or more selected clips play sound |
| Add Action | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| Speed… | The selection includes a clip that plays a media file |
| Speed Ramp… | Exactly one clip is selected and it plays a media file |
| Close Gap | There is a current track and the timeline has clips |
| Remove Silences… | Some clip plays sound |
| Remove Filler Words… | Some clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on |
| Transition ▸ items | A kind: a selected clip has room for a transition. **None**: something is selected |
| Motion ▸ items | A selected clip shows a picture |
| Look ▸ items | A selected clip shows a picture from a file, or is an adjustment clip |
| Add Background ▸ | Always |
| Add Blurred Background | Exactly one clip is selected and it has a picture size: a video, image, still, shape or graphic clip. Dimmed for a nest, text, adjustment or audio-only clip |
| Rename…, Label ▸ | Something is selected |
| Nest | Something is selected, other than a single nest clip on its own |
| Un-nest | The selection includes a nest clip |
| Open Nest | Exactly one clip is selected and it is a nest clip |
| Close Nest | A nest is open |

Open Nest and Close Nest are also greyed while you are typing in a text
field.

*Agents:* `split`, `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `freeze_frame`, `detach_audio`, `attach_audio`,
`normalize_clip`, `sync_audio`, `add_action`, `set_speed`, `add_speed_ramp`,
`close_gap`, `detect_silence`, `detect_fillers`, `add_transition` /
`set_transition`, `set_video` (motion and look), `add_background`,
`add_blurred_background`, `set_clip` (name and label), `nest`, `unnest`,
`set_scope` (open and close a nest).

## Track menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| New Track | ⇧⌘N | Adds a track |
| Remove Track | | Removes the current track. If it still holds clips, you are asked first |
| Remove Empty Tracks | | Removes every track that has no clips |
| Hide Video | | Hides the current track's picture |
| Mute Audio | | Mutes the current track's sound |
| Lock Track | | Locks the current track so its clips can't be edited |
| Solo | | Plays only this track's sound. A checkmark shows when it is on |
| Mix… | | Opens the current track's mix panel: volume, pan, compressor and limiter ([Audio](audio.md#track-volume-and-pan)) |
| Matte ▸ Off · Alpha · Inverted Alpha · Luma · Inverted Luma | | Makes the current track a matte that cuts the track behind it. A checkmark shows the track's mode ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)) |

These items act on the current track. To act on a particular track, use that
track's context menu ([below](#context-menus)).

*Agents:* `add_track`, `remove_track`, `remove_empty_tracks`, `set_track`
(hidden, muted, locked, solo, matte, volume, pan), `move_track`.

## Mark menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Add Marker | M (key) | Adds a marker at the playhead |
| Set In | I (key) | Sets the in point at the playhead |
| Set Out | O (key) | Sets the out point at the playhead |
| Clear Range | ⌥X | Clears the in/out range |
| Next Marker | | Moves the playhead to the next marker |

The marker items are off while a nest is open. Next and Previous Marker
also need the project to have markers, and Clear Range needs a range to be
set. See [The timeline](timeline.md).

*Agents:* `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `remove_marker`, `set_range` (with no
bounds it clears the range).

## View menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Zoom In | ⌘+ or ⌘= | Zooms the preview canvas in one step |
| Zoom Out | ⌘- | Zooms it out one step |
| Zoom to Fit | ⌘0 | Fits the canvas to the preview again |
| Fit Timeline | ⇧Z (key) | Zooms the timeline to show the whole project |
| Snapping | N (key) | Turns snapping on or off. A checkmark shows when it is on |
| Safe Areas | | Shows or hides the safe-area guides on the canvas |
| Hide Inspector | ⌥⌘I | Hides the inspector. The item is called **Show Inspector** while it is hidden |
| Assistant | ⌃⌘A | Shows the inspector's Assistant tab and puts the cursor in its message field ([Assistant](assistant.md)) |
| Timeline Track Height ▸ Small · Medium · Large | | Sets the height of the timeline rows |
| Preview Quality ▸ Full · Half · Quarter | | The preview's render size while you play. Export is not affected |
| Preview Window | ⇧⌘P | A second window showing the picture without overlays. Choose it again to close the window |
| Show Ungraded | ⌃⌘U | Shows the preview as if no clip were graded |
| Show Selection | | Shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. Needs a selected adjustment clip to turn on |
| Show SDR Version | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version ([HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md)) |
| Scopes | ⌃⌘W | Shows the scopes panel beside the preview ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Loudness Meter | ⌃⌘L | Shows the live loudness column beside the preview: momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and the true peak of what plays ([Audio](audio.md#live-loudness)) |

The canvas zoom steps are Fit, 50 %, 100 % and 200 %. View ▸ Zoom In, Zoom
Out and Zoom to Fit always act on the canvas. Zoom In is greyed at 200 %,

bar's controls or the gestures [below](#timeline-gestures). Show Ungraded,
Show SDR Version, Scopes and Loudness Meter are always enabled. Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector,
Timeline Track Height and Preview Quality are remembered between launches.

remembered, and they never change an export.

content.content: # Editing clips This page covers the edits you make to clips and to time on the timeline: putting clips on it, moving and trimming them, cutting, deleting and closing gaps, copying and pasting, and grouping clips into nests. Each edit is one undo step, and a gesture counts as one edit however long the drag lasts. When the project's rules won't allow an edit, the app beeps, changes nothing and tells you why. Changing a clip's speed, freezing a frame and reversing a clip are covered in [Speed](speed.md). Transitions are covered in [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md). Selecting, zooming, scrubbing and the track headers are covered in [Timeline](timeline.md). ## What an edit acts on Most commands act on the **selection**, the clips outlined in coral on the timeline. Some also use the **playhead**, the **in/out range**, or the **current track**: - **The selection.** Click a clip to select it. ⇧-click adds a clip or takes it out. Drag from empty space to select by marquee. ⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select All**), ⌥⌘A (**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead**, every clip that starts at or after the playhead) and **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** also select. ⌥-clicking a track header selects every clip on that track. See [Timeline](timeline.md). - **The playhead.** Split, trim to playhead, freeze frame, paste, insert and overwrite all work at the playhead. - **The in/out range.** I sets the in point, O sets the out point and ⌥X clears both (**Mark ▸ Set In / Set Out / Clear Range**). With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range instead. - **The current track** is the track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. Close Gap, Select All on Track, and Insert / Overwrite at Playhead use it. Clips on a **locked** track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled. A marquee skips them, and the edits that shift everything later in time leave them where they are. See [Limits](#limits). *Agents:* `set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the same view state. They are not edits and make no undo step. ## Adding clips from the Media tab Drag a file's row from the Media tab onto a track. What the drop does depends on the modifier keys you hold **when you release**: | Drop | What it does | Undo name | |---|---|---| | No modifier | Places the whole file as a clip at the drop point. Nothing else moves. The drop is refused if the clip would overlap its neighbours in a way the overlap rule forbids. | Add Clip | | ⌥ | **Insert.** Splits the clip under the drop point on that track, pushes everything on every unlocked track later by the file's length, then places the file in the gap. Only the destination track is cut. Clips on other tracks that span the drop point stay where they are, uncut; only clips that start at or after it move later. The exception is a detached sound linked to a clip that is cut: it is cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step. | Insert | | ⇧⌥ | **Overwrite.** Clears the file's length from the drop point on that track alone, cutting at both ends and removing what lies between, then places the file. Nothing moves and no other track is touched, except that a detached sound linked to a clip that is cut is cut at the same points; its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked. | Overwrite | Dropping a row on the **preview canvas** adds the file at the playhead on a new track at the front. The same two placements also work without dragging. Select a row in the Media tab, then choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**. They place the file on the current track at the playhead. Neither has a shortcut. Right-clicking a row gives you the same two items for that file. Both are greyed out when no media row is selected, and for a `.cube` LUT, which is applied as a look rather than placed (see [Colour grading](color-grading.md)). A new clip covers the whole file, rounded down to whole frames so it never runs past the end of the file. Footage larger than the canvas is fitted when the project's fit-new-clips setting is on. Importing files is covered in [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md). *Agents:* `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` take `track`, `media` and `at`. ## Moving clips Drag a clip's body to move it in time. Drag it up or down to move it to another track. If several clips are selected, dragging any one of them moves them all and keeps their timing and track offsets. Starts stop at zero. - **Onto a new track:** drop above the top lane to make a new front track, or below the bottom lane to make a new back track. - **Duplicate while dragging:** hold ⌥ when you press. Copies are dragged and the originals stay put (undo name "Duplicate Clips"). - **Refused drops spring back.** If the drop breaks the overlap rule (see [Limits](#limits)), the clip animates back to where it was and nothing changes. While you drag, positions the project refuses are skipped, and the clip stays at the last allowed position. - **Overlaps make transitions.** A clip dropped so it overlaps the clip before it on the same track gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Clips never push each other out of the way. Other edits do the same; see [Overlaps make transitions](#overlaps-make-transitions). The whole drag is one undo step, "Move Clips". ### Nudging `,` and `.` move the selection one frame earlier or later. With ⇧ they move it ten frames. A nudge is an ordinary move, so the overlap rule can refuse it (undo name "Nudge Clips"). *Agents:* `move_clip` takes `clips` and a `delta` in ticks. The optional `track` is the destination track for the first clip; the others keep their track offsets from it. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks. ## Trimming Drag either edge of a clip to trim it. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip: the pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and the selected clip shows trim grips. A clip too narrow on screen (under about 21 points) has no edges, so zoom in to trim it. Clips on locked tracks show no resize cursor. - A **start trim** moves the clip's start and its in point together, so the frame under the edge stays put and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline. - An **end trim** moves the clip's end. ## Splitting picture from sound **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (⌥⌘D) switches off each selected clip's sound and adds an audio-only copy of it on the track below, at the same time, with the same footage and speed. If the clip is on the back track, a new track is added behind it. Undo name: "Detach Audio". The two clips stay linked: moving, splitting, rippling, nesting or copying either one takes the other, and trimming the sound's edge alone makes a J-cut or an L-cut ([Audio](audio.md#j-cuts-and-l-cuts)). **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (⇧⌥⌘D) merges each pair back into one clip. Undo name: "Attach Audio". Each clip that can't be detached is refused with a reason: "clip … has no audio to detach: it is not a media clip", "…: media … has no audio track", or "…: its audio is switched off". A clip's picture and sound can each be switched on or off. The app's only control for this is Detach Audio. Agents can set either half directly. *Agents:* `detach_audio` takes `clip`, and `attach_audio` takes either half's `clip`. `set_enabled` takes `clip` and `video` and/or `audio` (true or false). Leave one out to keep its value. ## Nests A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on, the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing. ### Making and opening up a nest **Clip ▸ Nest** (⌘G) groups the selected clips: - The new nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used. It runs from the earliest start to the latest end and is selected afterwards. - Inside the nest, the clips keep their properties, actions and transitions, their timing relative to each other, and their stacking order. - The nest's own canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the project size later doesn't re-lay out what's inside. To change a nest's size, un-nest it (⇧⌘G), change the project size if you need to, and nest again (⌘G). Opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size. - It's named "Nest 1", "Nest 2", and so on. Double-clicking a nest clip opens it, so rename a nest clip with ⇧⌘R (**Clip ▸ Rename…**) or the Clip tab's name field. - Greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip. Refused when the nest clip would break the overlap rule, and when the selection holds an adjustment clip, which can't go inside a nest. **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (⇧⌘G) opens every selected nest clip back out, in one undo step, and selects what came out: - The clips return to the timeline at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added. - A clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new front track instead of being lost. - A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back. Trimming a nest hides content but doesn't cut it. - Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, open the nest and edit inside it (below). ### Editing inside a nest You can edit a nest's contents in place instead of un-nesting: - **Go in:** double-click a nest clip, or select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (⌘↓). - **Come out one level:** **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (⌘↑). - **Breadcrumb:** while a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as "Timeline › Intro". It shows the last two levels, and hovering it shows the full path. Clicking it goes out one level, like ⌘↑. Nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep. Open Nest needs exactly one nest clip selected, and Close Nest is greyed out at the top level. Both are greyed out while you are typing in a field. ### Shared and independent copies Split, Duplicate (⌘D) and ⌥-drag copies of a nest clip share one nest. Editing inside any of them changes them all, and the nest is only removed once no clip shows it. Copy and Paste make an independent copy, so editing a pasted nest leaves the original alone. Inside, the timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips from the nest's own zero. The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position or scale, so you edit the group on its own terms. The playhead is mapped in and out, so the frame under it doesn't change. When you go in, the selection is cleared. When you come out, the nest clip is selected again. Going in and coming out aren't edits: there is no undo step, and the project isn't marked as changed. The in/out range is cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. Every clip edit on this page works inside a nest, and each one is still one undo step on the project's single undo history. Some things belong to the whole project rather than to a nest: - **Markers.** Add Marker and Next / Previous Marker are greyed out inside a nest. A nest has no markers of its own. - **Media and project settings.** Adding, relinking or removing media and changing the Document tab still work with a nest open. They change the whole project. - **Adjustment clips.** **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out inside a nest. Some limits count the whole project even while you edit inside a nest: up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and the eight-level nesting depth. An edit that is fine inside the nest can still be refused when the whole project would go over one of them. *Agents:* `nest` takes `clips` and an optional `name`. `unnest` takes `clip`. Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, which applies the edit inside that nest using the nest's own ids and times. Nine edits are an error with a scope: the three marker edits, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` and `add_adjustment_clip`. `set_scope` opens a nest in the window itself, so that `get_project` and `render_frame` show its contents. It is view state, not an undo step. ## Removing empty tracks **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** removes every track that holds no clips. If every track is empty, the back-most track stays. Other track commands are covered in [Timeline](timeline.md). *Agents:* `remove_empty_tracks`. ## Limits - **The overlap rule.** On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests that would break it are refused. Paste and Un-nest put such clips on a new front track instead. Ripple deletes are never refused by it: a clip a ripple slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve (below). - **Overlaps make transitions.** Any edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it on its track gives it a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition: moves, trims, duplicates, pastes, ripple deletes, Close Gap, Nest and Un-nest. See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md). - **Locked tracks.** Their clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and a marquee doesn't select them. Split with nothing selected, Lift, and the range form of Ripple Delete leave them uncut. Ripples, gap closes and inserted time don't shift them. Insert onto a locked track and Close Gap on a locked track are refused. A clip on a locked track that you select by clicking is still removed by Delete or Ripple Delete, and Overwrite still clears a locked track. - **One frame minimum.** Trims and rolls always leave a clip at least one frame long. - **Footage bounds.** A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. - **Project size.** Up to 4,096 clips, 64 tracks and eight levels of nesting. - **Times are frames.** Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid.

# HDR and colour management

Frame Job reads each source as what it is: iPhone HDR video, HDR10 files, wide-gamut footage and camera log. It converts each one into the project's working colour before any grade, key or blend touches it. A project works in **SDR** (Rec. 709, the default) or in **HDR (HLG)** (Rec. 2100 HLG over BT.2020). An HDR project exports an HLG master, an HDR10 file or an SDR version, and you can preview that SDR version at any time. This page covers telling Frame Job how a file was shot, choosing the project's dynamic range and its blending, and the depth and colour you get in exports and saved frames.

Grading itself (Light, Color, curves, looks and the scopes) is covered in [Colour grading](color-grading.md). The export sheet as a whole is covered in [Export](export.md).

## How sources are read

You don't need to set anything for most footage. Each frame is converted once, at the very start of the picture pipeline, into the project's working colour. The chroma key and every grade then see the converted picture.

| Source | In an SDR project | In an HDR (HLG) project |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary Rec. 709 or untagged video, stills, recordings | Drawn as is | Lifted to HDR reference white (203 cd/m², HLG 75 %), so it looks the same as it does in SDR |
| HLG video (e.g. iPhone HDR) | Converted to Rec. 709 by Frame Job, highlights rolled off smoothly | Kept as HLG, highlights above white intact |
| PQ / HDR10 video or stills | Converted to Rec. 709, highlights rolled off at the file's own peak (see [HDR10 peak](#hdr10-peak)) | Real HDR: display light up to 1,000 cd/m², brighter highlights rolled off to fit |
| Wide-gamut SDR (BT.2020 or P3 primaries with an SDR transfer, sRGB included) | Converted to Rec. 709; colours outside Rec. 709 are eased toward their brightness and rolled off instead of clipped | Converted into BT.2020 and lifted |
| Camera log (set in the Media tab) | Converted to a normal-looking Rec. 709 picture | Converted to real HDR |
| Text, captions, shapes, graphics, the background colour | Drawn as is | Lifted to HDR reference white with the SDR sources |

The conversion is Frame Job's own. It works the same way in the preview, in every export, in rendered and saved frames, and in the timeline's filmstrip and the Media tab's thumbnails. Changing a file's Camera Log redraws its thumbnails. An HLG or PQ still's thumbnail appears once its converted tile is ready, a moment after import.

**View ▸ Show Ungraded** (⌃⌘U) turns off the grades, but this source conversion stays on. The conversion is how the file is read, not part of the grade.

## Camera log

Log footage looks flat and grey until it is converted. The **Camera Log** section of the **Media** tab tells Frame Job which curve a video file was shot with. The section appears once the project has a video file.

1. Open the **Media** tab in the inspector and click the file in the list.
2. Choose a curve from the **Log** popup.

It is a setting on the *file*, so every clip of that file follows it, reversed clips included. It is one undo step, **Camera Log**. A line under the popup says what is set. It reads "Select a video in the list" when the selected row is not a video file, and the popup is disabled. The section's header shows the selected file's setting (its curve or LUT name), so you can read it with the section collapsed.

Relinking a file (**Relink…**) keeps its Camera Log setting.

### The Log popup

| Item | Curve | Camera gamut |
|---|---|---|
| None | No conversion: shows the log picture as recorded | — |
| Apple Log | Apple Log | BT.2020 |
| Apple Log 2 | Apple Log | Apple Wide Gamut |
| S-Log3 / S-Gamut3.Cine | Sony S-Log3 | S-Gamut3.Cine |
| S-Log3 / S-Gamut3 | Sony S-Log3 | S-Gamut3 |
| V-Log / V-Gamut | Panasonic V-Log | V-Gamut |
| C-Log2 / Cinema Gamut | Canon Log 2 | Cinema Gamut |
| C-Log2 / BT.2020 | Canon Log 2 | BT.2020 |
| C-Log3 / Cinema Gamut | Canon Log 3 | Cinema Gamut |
| C-Log3 / BT.2020 | Canon Log 3 | BT.2020 |
| LUT: *name* | Each `.cube` LUT already in the project | — |
| Use LUT… | Choose a `.cube` file that converts this file's log to Rec. 709 | — |

Each built-in curve follows its maker's published curve and gamut; Cinema Gamut's primaries come from the ACES project's Canon transform. Frame Job's display transform puts 18 % grey at 42 % and 90 % white at about 78 %. Highlights roll off smoothly up to about six stops over grey. In an HDR (HLG) project the same footage becomes real HDR, with 18 % grey at HLG 38 % and no roll-off.

Whether a log file is stored in video range or full range is read from the file itself.

### Detection on import

An iPhone **Apple Log** or **Apple Log 2** file is recognised by its label when you import it, so it looks like normal video straight away. The line under the popup then adds "— from the file", for example "Apple Log — from the file". Sony, Panasonic and Canon files carry no label Frame Job can read, so choose their curve by hand. To see an Apple Log file's raw log picture, choose **None**.

### Using your own LUT
## Limits

- **Log detection is Apple-only.** Only Apple Log and Apple Log 2 are recognised on import. S-Log3, V-Log and Canon Log must be chosen by hand.
- **One setting per file.** Camera Log and the HDR10 peak belong to the media file, not to a clip. Two clips of one file can't be read differently.
- **The HDR10 peak is read once, at import.** Relinking a PQ file does not read its peak again; set it by hand if the new file differs. Relinking keeps the file's Camera Log.
- **Camera Log needs a video file.** It is refused on an audio file, an image or a LUT. A PQ still takes only a peak.
- **A peak only on a PQ file.** Setting a peak on a file that isn't PQ is refused.
- **A camera LUT as a look over Camera Log converts twice.** The Look section only warns.
- **The chroma key after switching to HDR (HLG) is close, not exact,** on HLG footage with P3 or BT.709 primaries, on PQ highlights above 1,000 cd/m² and on an HDR gain-map photo. Re-pick the key if an edge changes.
- **Some Canon files look too contrasty.** A non-ProRes Canon file flagged as video range that actually stores full-range codes looks too contrasty after C-Log2 or C-Log3 conversion.
- **Two settings are fixed.** There is no Dolby Vision output, and SDR reference white in an HDR project is fixed at 203 cd/m².
- **Wide-gamut SDR projects aren't offered.** An SDR project always works in Rec. 709.
# Driving Frame Job from an AI agent (MCP)

Frame Job serves its whole editor as MCP tools, so an AI agent such as
Claude Code can open projects, cut, style, check its work frame by frame and
export, the same way you do in the window. Every edit an agent makes goes
through the same place your own clicks go: it shows in the window at once,
marks the document edited, and can be undone with ⌘Z. This page covers
connecting a client, how calls behave, and the full list of tools.

## How an agent reaches Frame Job

Frame Job listens on a local Unix socket that it opens every time it
launches:

```
~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock
```

The socket serves MCP as streamable HTTP: each request is one JSON-RPC
`POST /mcp`, answered with a single JSON response. A client that can speak
HTTP over a Unix socket can connect to it directly. Most MCP clients start
a stdio server instead, and for them the bundle carries **framejob-mcp**, a
small stdio MCP server:

```
Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp
```

The helper does three things:

- **It starts a session without opening Frame Job.** It answers
  `initialize` and `ping` itself, and none of `initialize`, `ping` or
  `tools/list` ever launches the app.
- **It lists the tools even when Frame Job cannot answer.** `tools/list`
  asks the running app first. When the app is not running, or does not
  answer within 5 seconds (for example while another client's long call
  holds it), the helper answers from a copy of the catalog stored in the
  bundle, so a client can start up and see every tool with nothing on
  screen.
- **It opens Frame Job on the first tool call.** If a call finds the app
## Limits

- Only programs running as you can connect, and only while Frame Job is
  running (the helper launches it for a call).
- Calls run one at a time. A long call — an export's start is quick, but a
  recording or a transcription is not — holds the next one until it ends,
  and any call waits while you hold the mouse down mid-drag.
- If Frame Job launches but does not start listening within 60 seconds, the
  call is answered with that, and later calls in the same client session do
  not launch another copy; quit the stray copy and try again.
- A tool call never asks you anything, so anything that needs a question
  answered or a system grant given has to be done by a person first.
- Copy MCP Command writes the Claude Code command only; other clients take
  the helper's path by hand.

docs/guide/export.md:117:- For **AV1** the rate is a soft cap. AV1 encodes at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate, so it usually stays under the rate and simple footage comes out much smaller. Very detailed footage can go over: up to about 1.25 times the rate was measured. Its tier titles and footnote read `usually ≤ …`.
docs/guide/export.md:118:- For **VP9 (WebM)** the rate is a soft cap the same way: VP9 encodes at a constant quality chosen to match or beat HEVC at that rate (HEVC 10-bit's in an HDR export), and the file usually stays under it. Up to about 1.15 times the rate was measured. Its tier titles and footnote read `usually ≤ …` too. On **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** the rate is the picture's alone: the transparency is a second stream at a fixed quality that comes on top of it, so the file is larger than the rate says. In the measured exports of a moving soft-edged shape the transparency was about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, about 9–21 % at 720p and about 21–39 % at 640 × 360 (the higher figure at the Low tier); a smaller picture keeps its edges clean with a larger share.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`

  ignoring case, ordered, named (`Track N`, `/` and `:` as `-`, ` (Track N)`

- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the twelve `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the

  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An

  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the

  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts

  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/

  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`

- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s

  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>
