- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,

  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and

  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its

  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map

  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.

  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).

  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,

  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under

  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s

  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view

  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked

  §11 G-35): `prores_4444`'s in place in float, `hevc_alpha`'s rounded first
  into a pooled 32BGRA buffer (`ExportFrames`, `ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`,
  PR-3); the fill is one generic pass over `StraightAlphaLayout` (`BGRA8`,
  `RGBAHalf`), whose `allVisible` keeps the whole-row check vectorised.
  `h264`'s and `hevc`'s frames are rounded to 8 bits the same way and not
  straightened, and `hevc` is pinned to Main; `hevc_10bit` maps to `.hevc`
  too, is told apart by its codec name (`isMain10`), is pinned to Main 10
  and, like every other row, gets the frame as drawn.
  `ExportWriter` FILLS the frame when a fit would leave at most
  a pixel uncovered, or — the frame a canvas-SHAPED size less at most one
  pixel on each axis, `(bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw` for some `a`, `b` in
  {0, 1}, at any scale — when a fill would overshoot by at most one
  (`shapeGap`: `gap <= limit`, in integers), and letterboxes past that, where
  an alpha-carrying movie row (`prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`) is refused instead
  (padding inverts the alpha; a pure scale is fine); so no size of the
  canvas's own shape is refused for being odd, and a typed size of another
  shape is judged as the even frame it becomes; the frame is the size the
  CORE resolved, already even where the row needs it (spec §11 G-33), and
  `encodedSize` is only the floor under it; a missing encoder is
  `.presetUnavailable` and no file (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`, in
  `ExporterErrors.swift`, applied where `startWriting` hears the pipeline); `apng` FITS instead and must not
  grow the guard. GIF and APNG refuse past 600 frames rather than truncate.
  `renderFrame` is documented off-main. Audio export is NOT bit-deterministic
  within an 8 ms window at a duck ramp edge (AVFoundation's mix); a duck-free
  project decodes byte-identical. `ExportError` is `ExporterErrors.swift`'s.
  An export PINS the `GraphicSet` it was handed for its whole life, GATES it
  before the build (`ExporterGraphics.graphicsRefusal`: a graphic clip in
  the range, or in any nest reached from one, however deep, whose module did
  not compile or is missing, refuses before the destination is touched), and
  ABORTS on a recorded failure: `pollProgress` cancels and `finish` removes
  the file and answers `.graphicFailed`, whatever the pipeline said.
  `startWriting` starts the graphic prefetch (`startGraphicPrefetch`, G-26)
  after the pipeline is picked, and `releaseRecipeKey` (from `finish` and
  `deinit`) `stop`s it on the line before the `unpin`, then releases the
  export's ramp-audio wants — dispatched off the caller's thread from
  `deinit`, which can run inside `RampAudioRenders.wait`'s lock.
  `Exporter.graphicWarnings` (`ExporterGraphics.swift`'s
  `ExportGraphicWarning`, each (name, message) once with its first frame) is
  published in `finish` before the unpin and read by the progress sheet
  (count on the line, list in the tooltip), the queue (`Job.graphicWarnings`;
  the count right after "Exported “…”." since the row truncates its tail;
  `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)`) and `export`'s `graphic_warnings`
  (G-24 (c)).
  **`ExportWriter.cancel()` and `Exporter.cancel()` only set flags**; the
  measurement's loop cancels its own reader, `ExportWriter` reads each output
  on a reader of its own and each pump cancels its own reader on its own queue
  after its own last read (spec §11 #378), and the writer is cancelled in
  `allInputsFinished`, after every pump has left its loop — cancelling a
  reader under a running `copyNextSampleBuffer` crashed the process. Never
  call `cancelReading` from another thread while a loop reads; a read that
  never returns for another reason is not woken (spec §11 G-17).
- `DeepStillFrame.swift` — whether a frame's recipe draws a still deeper than
  8 bits (`shows`), and `read`: a deep frame through export's reader
  (`AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` at `64RGBAHalf`), spec §11 PR-9 and
  PR-12; its image is in `FrameWriter.frameSpace` (§11 PR-11).
- `DeepVideoFrame.swift` — the one question `Exporter.renderFrameReported`
  asks after the build when its caller passes `keepsDepth` (`carriesDepth`:
  `render_frame` and Save Frame… as PNG or HEIC): `reads` is PR-9's deep still
  or `shows`, a recipe `track` layer whose composition segment at the frame
  time reads a VP9 file whose `vpcC` bitDepth is above 8 (`isDeep`), spec §11
  PR-12.
- `FrameWriter.swift` — a `CGImage` and a format in, a URL out, no panel:
  Save Frame and `render_frame` both call `writeFrame`, so their PNGs are
  byte-identical by construction; `writeFrame` labels a rendered frame BT.709
  (`frameSpace`, §11 PR-11; `labelled` does the same for an APNG's frames;
  an HLG project's frame is `hlgSpace`, BT.2100 HLG, and JPEG is refused for
  it, HD-13), `pickable` relabels an HLG frame so a pick reads its raw
  values, and `write` is for snapshots, sheets and tiles. PNG keeps a NIL properties

content.text: I have enough to answer. Returning the inventory.

capabilities: Open a movie, sound or picture and get an untitled project sized and timed to it: a portrait phone clip opens portrait, and 29.97/23.976 rates are kept exactly (docs/guide/projects-and-media.md).
A project is a .framejob package. Media is referenced (path plus bookmark); Consolidate Media copies it in; macOS autosave and Revert To versions apply.

Imports what macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, VP9 Profile 0/2, AV1 on M3 or later, and stills including HEIC and WebP. WebM and MKV are rewrapped into a .mov with no re-encode (core/src/container*.rs). An ffmpeg fallback is used only if ffmpeg is already installed.
Missing-media sheet with folder-wide Locate; per-file Relink…; Camera Log and HDR10 peak set per media file.

The canvas can be changed at any time: presets 1080p, 4K, 720p, Vertical 1080×1920, Square, 1440p, Source Size, or custom even sizes up to 16384. Frame rate can change too (all clip and marker times are re-snapped). 'Resize clips proportionally' rescales placements (core/src/edit_canvas.rs).
Media tab: search by name, sort by import order, name, duration or kind, an 'Unused only' filter, Reveal in Timeline/Finder, Remove with or without its clips.
limits: No bins, folders, tags, ratings, favourites or keywords in the Media tab (#112 iceboxed).
No source viewer: a placed clip is always the whole file, and in/out are set by trimming on the timeline. There is no skimming in the browser.

Only the FIRST audio track of a file is used (app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift firstTrack; core/src/container.rs reads the first video and audio track). A multitrack OBS, Zoom or recorder file loses tracks 2 and up.
A project has one canvas. A vertical version means Duplicate plus set_canvas plus manual repositioning, and a nest's canvas stays frozen at the size it was nested at.
Caps: 4,096 clips, 64 tracks, 1,024 media, nests 8 deep.
No proxy or optimized media.

capabilities: One kind of track that holds any clip; per-track hide, mute, lock, solo; per-track volume, pan, compressor and limiter; matte mode.

Move, nudge, trim, rate-stretch (⌥-drag), slip, roll, split, lift, ripple delete (selection or range), close gap, insert time, insert and overwrite (⌥ / ⇧⌥ drop), duplicate, copy/cut/paste, Paste Attributes, nests with open-in-place and a breadcrumb.
Detach Audio keeps picture and sound linked, so J- and L-cuts stay in sync through edits; Attach Audio puts them back.

Filmstrips and waveforms, a frame-accurate ruler, JKL shuttle, snapping, markers (chapter flag), an in/out range, loop, clip names and colour labels, a second Preview Window for another display, Preview Quality Full/Half/Quarter, scrub audio.
Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point. A refused edit says the rule's own sentence.
limits: There is no magnetic or storyline mode; an overlap automatically becomes a cross dissolve.
Markers exist only on the top-level timeline, and a marker's colour can be set only by an agent.
Timeline zoom has no keyboard shortcut except ⇧Z (fit).

capabilities: Move, scale, rotate and crop on the canvas, with snapping to edges, centres and thirds; safe-area guides (90/80 %).
Opacity, 8 blend modes, corner radius, drop shadow, reflection, up to 4 filters (blur, sharpen, pixelate, sepia, noir, vignette, invert).
Chroma key with Pick from Canvas, tolerance, softness and spill.
Spotlight: dim outside a rectangle or ellipse, with optional magnify. Obscure: up to 4 blurred or pixelated regions per clip for privacy, drawn on the canvas.

Text clips with any installed font plus 7 bundled faces, outline, backdrop, auto or fixed-width box, Typewriter/Word Fade/Line Rise reveals, inline canvas editing, and 4 presets (Title, Subtitle, Lower Third, Caption).
Shape clips: rectangle, ellipse, line, arrow, with linear or radial gradients up to 8 stops.
Backgrounds: solid, image, or Add Blurred Background (a blurred fill copy, the vertical-video backdrop).
Matte tracks (Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma, Inverted Luma): any clip on the track, including text, shapes, graphics and video, cuts the track behind it.
limits: No pen or bezier mask tool and no per-clip mask; masking means a matte track or a JS graphic drawing a path.
No motion tracking: regions follow the layer's own transform, never what is in the picture.
Scale is uniform for pictures.
Text presets are 4 hard-coded entries (app/Sources/TextPane.swift TextPreset.all); there are no user-saved text styles.

capabilities: Actions: a span on a clip that eases its properties to an end state along a curve (Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out). Almost everything animates: transform, crop, filters, regions, every grade control, every audio setting, text style, graphic properties, and speed (which is how speed ramps work). Colours blend in OKLab.
An action lane on each clip, both on the timeline and in the Clip tab, with drag, resize and ◆ ◇ ○ ⊘ row marks.
Zoom to Region (Z) draws a rectangle and makes an eased zoom to it; Zoom Back returns. Both are aimed at screencasts.
Motion presets: In and Out (Fade, Zoom In/Out, 4 slides, Spin, Pop) and During (Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce, Drift), tied to the clip's ends.

13 transitions (cross dissolve, fade through black or white, 4 pushes, 5 wipes, slide, zoom) with curve, crossfade on/off and 4 crossfade shapes. Clip ▸ Transition at a hard cut builds the overlap from unused handles.
limits: No independent keyframe track per property, no graph or bezier easing editor, and actions on one clip cannot overlap.
Shape styling, ducking, fade shapes, the voice effect, and track volume/pan cannot be animated.
No motion blur and no auto-animate.

capabilities: Constant speed ×0.1 to ×1000, Fit to a length, ⌥-drag rate stretch, Keep pitch, reverse (rendered in the background), freeze frame.
Speed ramps as actions; Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… gives Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip and Speed Burst in one step. Ramp audio is rendered offline. Captions follow speed changes.
limits: No optical-flow or frame-blend slow motion (frames are repeated or dropped).
Audio is dropped above ×12.
Keep pitch on a ramp can lag up to about 22 ms after a deep slow-down.

capabilities: A per-clip chain: voice isolation (Apple AUSoundIsolation, which also de-reverbs), 16 voice effects, channel pick, 7-slot EQ with voice presets, hum removal, noise reduction, gate, phrase-by-phrase leveller, de-esser, compressor, pan/mono, true-peak limiter, fades in 4 shapes, and a draggable volume line. All of it animates with actions.

Enhance Voice sets a whole voice chain from the clip's own measurements in one step; it can also run automatically when a recording lands. Match Audio copies loudness and speech EQ tone from a reference clip. Normalize goes to LUFS (−16 default) or to peak.
Ducking by clip length or by detected speech (pre-roll and hold).
Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by sound: MFCC speech matching, GCC-PHAT refinement, drift correction by tiny varispeed, and a weak-match confirmation sheet.
Track compressor and limiter (exact in export, approximate in preview); live loudness meter (momentary, short-term, integrated, true peak); scrub audio.
Export always passes a −1 dBTP true-peak master limiter; loudness targets −14, −16, −23 or custom; stems per track or per track name; 24-bit WAV/AIFF.
limits: No beat detection or music retime (#415, #416), no source separation (#417), no AI speech or TTS (#418), no spectrum analyser (#421), no hosting of third-party Audio Units.
No music or SFX library.
Voice isolation and voice effects play only on ×1 clips.
Only the first audio track of a multitrack file is used.

capabilities: Remove Silences: on-device Silero VAD (voice mode) or a level threshold, measured in the mix; it previews the cuts and makes them as one ripple across unlocked tracks.
Remove Filler Words: um/uh and the like cut on AssemblyAI word timings, widened to a 32 ms grid, one undo step. Captions never show fillers.
get_transcript: any clip's timed words (cached cloud transcript or on-device recogniser, cached per media). The Assistant uses it to cut false starts on request.
detect_silence and detect_fillers plus ripple_delete_ranges are exposed to agents.
limits: No text-editor transcript view where deleting words cuts the video; transcript cutting exists only through the Assistant or MCP.
Filler removal is cloud-only: on-device transcription kept 1 of 8 fillers in the owner's test (TR-7).
Cuts never reach into nests or transition overlaps.

capabilities: Generate Captions on this Mac (any installed Speech language, nothing uploaded, model downloadable in the sheet) or with AssemblyAI (BYO key, auto-detect plus 21 languages, speaker labels, vocabulary, cost estimate shown before upload, transcript cache, the service asked to delete its copy).

Two-line Subtitles, or 5 word-by-word short-form styles (Highlight, Pill, Karaoke, Build, One Word) sized to the shorter canvas side, with looks (Slide the pill, Fill words as spoken, Dim in pauses). Restyle with Replace reuses the cached transcript.
Captions are ordinary text clips and are burned in. Import SRT; export SRT or WebVTT per track, round-trip exact to the frame.
limits: No translation or dubbing (no Translation framework import); one language per run.
No soft-subtitle track in exported movies; WebVTT import is not supported.

No keyword emphasis, emoji or animated-emoji captions. Word-style colours have no inspector UI (agent set_text only). Speaker colours apply to Subtitles only, and speakers cannot be named (#192 icebox).

areas.area: Colour grading, HDR and colour management
capabilities: Color tab: Light (exposure, white balance and more), Color, Lift/Gamma/Gain wheels, curves (RGB plus Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat), 8 built-in looks, .cube LUT import, adjustment clips with HSL qualifiers (blur, Show Selection), Show Ungraded, scopes (waveform, parade, vectorscope with zoom, histogram). Every grade control animates.
Sources are read as what they are: iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ with its peak, wide-gamut SDR. Camera log curves: Apple Log and Apple Log 2 (auto-detected), S-Log3, V-Log, C-Log2/3, or your own LUT.
SDR (Rec. 709) or HDR (HLG) projects; HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables; Show SDR Version preview; opt-in linear-light blending; a 16-bit float compositor.
limits: No Dolby Vision output; no Offset wheel and no qualifier on picture clips (owner closed both as not wanted).
Only Apple Log is detected on import; S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log must be chosen by hand (#278).
No AI or auto colour match between cameras, and no shot-match.

capabilities: A graphic clip is a sandboxed QuickJS module that returns SVG per frame, rasterised by resvg. Properties become inspector controls and animate with actions.

23 bundled templates in the Graphic browser with a live looping preview: bar, line and donut charts; gauge, countdown, counter, progress bar; screencast arrow highlight, callout, keyboard keys, step badge, window frame; chapter card, kinetic type, logo reveal, lower third, news ticker, quote card, title card; social end screen, handle tag, social popup, subscribe button.
Share as a .fjgraphic package with only the fonts and pictures it uses; import by double-click. Agents can write, render (contact sheets) and place modules.
Graphics are prefetched on spare cores, background-rendered when idle, and capped at a quarter of RAM.
limits: A graphic cannot read video pixels (#251 icebox); video shows inside a graphic only through a matte track.
A heavy scene's first play falls behind: resvg takes about 279 ms per 1080p frame (#328, parked).
8-bit rasters (#374).
There is no visual template editor; a new graphic means JavaScript, or asking an agent.

capabilities: Records a display or one window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, the microphone as a separate file auto-aligned, click rings, 30/60 fps, points or pixels, and pause/resume as separate stretches. It lands in a new project or at the playhead of an open one.
Camera alone, or beside the screen as a bottom-right talking-head track (Continuity Camera supported, format picker, live preview).
Microphone-only voice-over at the playhead; 'Enhance the microphone when it lands'.
record_screen over MCP.
limits: The cursor and click rings are burned in (app/Sources/RecordingSetup.swift sets showsCursor and showMouseClicks). No cursor metadata is kept, so there is no auto-zoom that follows the cursor, no cursor smoothing, resizing or hiding, and no automatic keystroke overlay (the Keyboard keys graphic is typed by hand).
One camera only, no remote or guest recording, no iPhone screen capture, no 10-bit recording (PR-8 not wanted).

capabilities: H.264, HEVC 8-bit, 10-bit and with alpha; AV1 in MP4 or WebM (bundled SVT-AV1, 10-bit, HDR, 3 speeds, time estimate); VP9 WebM and VP9 with alpha (bundled libvpx, Opus audio); ProRes 422/4444; M4A, WAV and AIFF with stems; GIF and APNG; still frames as PNG, JPEG or HEIC.

Size rows follow the document's shape (a vertical 1080p is 1080×1920); quality tiers scaled from area and frame rate; loudness targets; burned-in timecode for review; saved presets; an Export Queue that runs while you keep editing, with a memory ledger for software encoders.
Chapter markers become embedded chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM. MP4 is written fast-start.
limits: No named platform presets (YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, Instagram) and no platform safe-zone overlays.
No upload or publish to any platform. File ▸ Share shares the project package, not the export.
No YouTube-description chapter list (the 00:00 text) and no thumbnail export preset.
Exports run one at a time; GIF and APNG are capped at 600 frames; 4K GIF/APNG uses 8–12 GB (#383).

capabilities: The whole editor as MCP tools over a local Unix socket: one tool per core op (64 op tools) plus app-state tools, 106 product tools in all (per CLAUDE.md). The bundled framejob-mcp stdio helper launches the app on first call; Settings has a one-click 'Copy MCP Command' for Claude Code.
render_frame lets an agent look at frames, including scope data; get_project returns the whole project JSON; every agent edit is a normal undo step, shown live in the window.

An in-app Assistant (Claude, BYO Anthropic key) in an inspector tab. It uses the same tools, asks before writing files, has cloud uploads and recording withheld, renders frames to check its visual edits, compacts long conversations, and shows per-turn, per-conversation and monthly spend from a LiteLLM price table.
limits: The Assistant has no built-in creator recipes (highlights, chapters, titles, descriptions, thumbnails, B-roll); it does only what the edit tools do, on request.
It cannot start paid cloud transcription itself and cannot record.
No speech input and no floating window (#160 icebox).

capabilities: Native Swift/AppKit with a Rust core; Apple Silicon on macOS 26 or later; Apache-2.0 open source; signed and notarized DMG releases; Sparkle auto-update.
No account and no backend: every cloud feature is bring-your-own-key (AssemblyAI, Anthropic).
A large automated proof suite: 240k lines of test and proof code against 107k lines of product code (README.md).
limits: Performance is documented only for 1080p: docs/manual-checks.md PB-2 'Playback holds 60 fps' on a 1080p movie. There is no measured 4K or multi-hour editing benchmark. Perf issues are parked by owner choice (features first).
The 8-concurrent-video-track decoder budget is a warning only (core/src/plan.rs MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS); playback drops frames past it.
No in-app tutorials on main yet (branch unmerged). Help ▸ Frame Job Help ships no help book.
From the owner's memory (2026-10-09, not in the repo): Frame Job had not yet been used for real work.

checked_absences.feature: Changing a project's aspect ratio / canvas size after it is made
checked_absences.evidence: docs/guide/projects-and-media.md 'The Document tab: canvas settings' (presets incl. Vertical 1080×1920 and Square, Width/Height, 'Resize clips proportionally'); core/src/edit_canvas.rs set_canvas and rescale(). x and y follow their own axis ratio and scale follows the SMALLER ratio, so 16:9→9:16 fits and letterboxes rather than fills. Action end states are not rescaled, and a nest's canvas stays frozen (docs/guide/editing.md 'Nests').

checked_absences.feature: Vertical (9:16) repurposing of a 16:9 edit; automatic reframing or subject tracking
checked_absences.evidence: Manual only. Vertical canvas preset; Fill Canvas button; Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background ('the usual backdrop for… a vertical video', docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md); Zoom to Region actions; word captions sized to the shorter side (docs/guide/captions.md). No Vision framework import anywhere in app/Sources, and 0 hits for reframe, VNTrack, Saliency or FaceRectangles in app/Sources, core/src or docs/guide. Auto-reframe is a spec §1 non-goal (designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md). One canvas per project.

checked_absences.feature: Social export presets (YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels sizes and bitrates)
checked_absences.evidence: docs/guide/export.md: Size rows Document/4K/1440p/1080p/720p follow the document's shape; Loudness '−14 LUFS (streaming)'; user-saved presets (app/Sources/ExportPresetsStore.swift); quality tiers scaled from YouTube's ladder (comments in app/Sources/ExportSheetOptions.swift). There are no named platform presets: 0 hits for TikTok or Instagram in app/Sources, and 'YouTube' appears only in loudness and bitrate comments.

0 hits for oauth or googleapis. Every 'upload' hit in app/Sources is AssemblyAI (AssemblyAIClient*.swift, CloudTranscriber*.swift, FillerTranscription.swift). File ▸ Share is the macOS share menu for the project package (docs/guide/projects-and-media.md).

checked_absences.feature: Project templates and brand kits (saved fonts/colours/logos/intros/outros)
checked_absences.evidence: 0 hits for 'brand kit', BrandKit or 'project template'. Text presets are 4 hard-coded entries (app/Sources/TextPane.swift TextPreset.all). The nearest pieces: File ▸ Duplicate of a project, saved export presets, and .fjgraphic packages that carry a graphic's fonts and pictures (docs/guide/graphics.md 'Sharing a graphic'); graphic fonts are imported per project.

4 text presets (docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md 'Text presets'); Subtitles plus 5 word-caption styles and 3 looks (docs/guide/captions.md 'Caption styles'); 23 graphic templates (docs/guide/graphics.md); 7 bundled fonts. No user-saved text or caption styles. Word-style colours have no inspector UI ('Generate again, or have an agent use set_text's word_style'). No keyword emphasis or emoji (captions.md Limits).

checked_absences.feature: Stock media, music or sound-effects library
checked_absences.evidence: 0 hits for stock, Pexels, Pixabay, 'sound effect' or 'music library' in app/Sources, core/src or docs/guide. The only bundled content is fonts, the Silero VAD model and the 23 graphic templates.

docs/guide/projects-and-media.md 'The Media tab': a flat list with Search by name, Sort (Import Order/Name/Duration/Kind) and Unused only, none of it saved. No bins, tags, ratings or keywords; #112 (icebox) asks whether a left-hand browser with bins is due. No source viewer: 'A new clip covers the whole file' (docs/guide/editing.md), and 0 hits for SourceViewer, SourceMonitor or skim.

docs/guide/motion-and-transitions.md 'Actions': spans with an end state and one of 4 curves; picture, grade, audio, text, graphic properties and speed all animate; colours blend in OKLab; actions on a clip may not overlap; core/src/actions.rs. Missing next to classic keyframes: independent per-property tracks, bezier easing and a graph editor; shape styling and track volume/pan cannot be animated.

Matte tracks (Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma, Inverted Luma) where any clip cuts the track behind it (docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md 'Matte tracks', core/src/model_matte.rs). Shapes are rectangle, ellipse, line and arrow; spotlight and obscure regions are rectangle or ellipse; a JS graphic can draw any SVG path as a matte (docs/guide/graphics.md 'Showing video inside a graphic'). 0 hits for bezier or Bezier; no pen tool and no per-clip mask.

checked_absences.feature: Motion tracking (attach text to a moving object)
checked_absences.evidence: 0 hits for VNTrack or track_object. The only 'tracker' in app/Sources is the noise-reduction minimum tracker (AudioNoiseReductionStage.swift). Obscure and spotlight regions are stored in source pixels and follow the layer's transform, not the content (canvas-and-layers.md 'Obscure').

0 hits for multicam, multi-cam or 'angle switch'. Multicam is a spec §1 non-goal (designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md). Building blocks that exist: Synchronize Audio (docs/guide/audio.md), nests, and one camera recorded beside the screen.

checked_absences.feature: Proxy media or optimized media for 4K/long projects
checked_absences.evidence: 0 proxy hits in app/Sources (the core/src hit is an mcp-proxy comment in mcp_versions.rs). Only View ▸ Preview Quality Full/Half/Quarter, which reduces render size, not decode (docs/guide/timeline.md 'Preview Quality'). core/src/plan.rs MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS = 8 is a warning only.

checked_absences.feature: Editing by transcript (a text editor that cuts the video)
checked_absences.evidence: Remove Silences, Remove Filler Words (cloud-only, TR-7), and get_transcript with the Assistant cutting false starts on request (docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md; app/Sources/TranscriptReader.swift, AgentServer+Transcript.swift). No transcript-view UI exists in app/Sources; designs/adr/cut-by-transcript.md TR-3/TR-5 route false starts through the assistant.

Chapter markers are placed by hand (docs/guide/timeline.md 'Markers'; add_marker {chapter}). Nothing generates titles or descriptions. The Assistant could add chapter markers from get_transcript if asked, but there is no feature or prompt for it.
0 hits for highlight detection or clip finding in app/Sources, core/src or docs/guide. The Assistant can only cut what it is told to, using get_transcript and ripple_delete_ranges.
No feature, no stock library, and nothing in docs/guide.

checked_absences.feature: Background removal without a green screen
checked_absences.evidence: #124 (icebox) 'Effects E9: Remove Background through Vision'. designs/adr/effects-survey.md says E3–E9 were deferred and E9 was planned on Vision, not the GPL RVM model. There is no `import Vision` in app/Sources. Chroma key exists.
0 hits for 'eye contact' or gaze in app/Sources, core/src or docs/guide.

0 hits for AVSpeechSynthesizer, TTS or text-to-speech. #418 is an audio candidate (AI speech, word regeneration, voice conversion). The 16 Voice Effects (docs/guide/audio.md 'Voice Effect') are Apple AU chains, not AI voices.

Transcription in many languages: on-device any installed Speech language, AssemblyAI auto-detect plus 21 (docs/guide/captions.md). One language per run, no `import Translation`, 0 hits for translate or dub. Cut dead air with Remove Silences (on-device VAD) and ums with Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI); have the Assistant cut false starts. Enhance Voice, Normalize to −14/−16 LUFS, use isolation, leveller and de-esser. Sync a separate recorder with Synchronize Audio. Grade with log conversion, LUTs and scopes. Punch in with Zoom to Region; add lower thirds, chapter cards, subscribe and end-screen graphics; caption on-device or in the cloud; set chapter markers that are embedded in the MP4; export H.264, HEVC or AV1 with a loudness target. distinctive_strengths: The whole editor as MCP tools (64 op tools printed from the core's own op table, 106 product tools in all) over a local socket, with a bundled stdio helper, one-click Copy MCP Command for Claude Code, render_frame so an agent can see its work, and every agent edit a normal undo step shown live. Few if any commercial NLEs offer this.

A built-in Claude Assistant on the user's own key that uses the same tools, renders frames to check visual edits, asks before writing files, withholds cloud uploads and recording, and shows per-turn and monthly cost.
Open source (Apache-2.0), no account and no backend; bring-your-own-key for both cloud services; on-device first (Speech, Silero VAD on Core ML, AUSoundIsolation).

A broadcast-grade audio chain rare in creator editors: phrase-level leveller, de-esser, gate, hum removal, EQ, voice isolation, an always-on true-peak master, LUFS targets, stems, one-click Enhance Voice and Match Audio, Synchronize Audio with drift correction, Duck by Speech, a live loudness meter.

A built-in recorder (screen, window, camera beside the screen, voice-over) feeding straight into the timeline, plus screencast tools: Zoom to Region, spotlight, obscure regions, and screencast graphics.

A programmable motion-graphics engine: JS modules drawing SVG per frame, 23 templates, properties as inspector controls and animatable, shareable .fjgraphic packages, and agents that can write new graphics on demand.

A serious colour and HDR pipeline in a creator app: log curves for Apple, Sony, Panasonic and Canon; HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables; a 16-bit float compositor; wheels, curves, hue curves, qualifiers, adjustment clips, LUTs, four scopes.
Codec breadth: bundled SVT-AV1 and libvpx (AV1 in MP4 and WebM, VP9 and VP9-with-alpha WebM for transparent web video), HEVC with alpha, ProRes 4444, APNG; WebM and MKV import without re-encode.
Word-by-word social captions (5 styles plus looks) on-device or via AssemblyAI with cost estimates and transcript caching; transcript-timed filler removal.
A native Swift/AppKit app with a Rust core, deterministic preview/export parity, and an unusually large automated proof suite.
non_goals: Spec §1 (designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md) non-goals, which the owner says may now be lifted: multicam; a plugin system (beyond JS graphic modules, G-1; hosting third-party Audio Units stays out); motion blur; stabilisation; optical-flow retiming; auto-reframe.
Any platform but macOS on Apple Silicon (macOS 26 or later).

Effects are closed, versioned vocabularies, with no runtime, user shaders or expression language (spec §11 R5-1, designs/adr/effects-survey.md D1). E3–E9 of the effects survey were deferred; E9 (Vision background removal) and E4 (13 filter kinds) are iceboxed (#124, #119).
No ffmpeg in the product (an optional user-installed ffmpeg is used only as an import fallback).
No relay, account or subscription backend; every AI feature is BYO key. A captions relay (#125) is iceboxed and the owner asks it not be raised again.
Assistant guardrails by design: it never records, never closes its own project, never starts paid cloud transcription, and asks before writing exports or saves.
Grading items closed as not wanted: Offset wheel (GR-27), qualifier on picture clips (GR-28), 1,024-level scopes (GR-29), histogram behind the curves (GR-30), wide-gamut SDR working space (GR-20).

Format items closed as not wanted: VP9 in MP4 and AV1 alpha (CX-1); 10-bit hevc_alpha and 10-bit screen recording (PR-8); Dolby Vision output and a fixed 203 cd/m² SDR white (hdr-and-color.md Limits).
No code, shaders or colour tables may be taken from Concat (AGPL).
Owner ordering: features before performance (perf issues parked in the 'Frame Job — Performance' project, e.g. #328).

capabilities: Open a movie, sound or picture and get an untitled project sized and timed to it: a portrait phone clip opens portrait, and 29.97/23.976 rates are kept exactly (docs/guide/projects-and-media.md).
A project is a .framejob package. Media is referenced (path plus bookmark); Consolidate Media copies it in; macOS autosave and Revert To versions apply.

Imports what macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, VP9 Profile 0/2, AV1 on M3 or later, and stills including HEIC and WebP. WebM and MKV are rewrapped into a .mov with no re-encode (core/src/container*.rs). An ffmpeg fallback is used only if ffmpeg is already installed.
Missing-media sheet with folder-wide Locate; per-file Relink…; Camera Log and HDR10 peak set per media file.

The canvas can be changed at any time: presets 1080p, 4K, 720p, Vertical 1080×1920, Square, 1440p, Source Size, or custom even sizes up to 16384. Frame rate can change too (all clip and marker times are re-snapped). 'Resize clips proportionally' rescales placements (core/src/edit_canvas.rs).
Media tab: search by name, sort by import order, name, duration or kind, an 'Unused only' filter, Reveal in Timeline/Finder, Remove with or without its clips.
limits: No bins, folders, tags, ratings, favourites or keywords in the Media tab (#112 iceboxed).
No source viewer: a placed clip is always the whole file, and in/out are set by trimming on the timeline. There is no skimming in the browser.

Only the FIRST audio track of a file is used (app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift firstTrack; core/src/container.rs reads the first video and audio track). A multitrack OBS, Zoom or recorder file loses tracks 2 and up.
A project has one canvas. A vertical version means Duplicate plus set_canvas plus manual repositioning, and a nest's canvas stays frozen at the size it was nested at.
Caps: 4,096 clips, 64 tracks, 1,024 media, nests 8 deep.
No proxy or optimized media.

capabilities: One kind of track that holds any clip; per-track hide, mute, lock, solo; per-track volume, pan, compressor and limiter; matte mode.

Move, nudge, trim, rate-stretch (⌥-drag), slip, roll, split, lift, ripple delete (selection or range), close gap, insert time, insert and overwrite (⌥ / ⇧⌥ drop), duplicate, copy/cut/paste, Paste Attributes, nests with open-in-place and a breadcrumb.
Detach Audio keeps picture and sound linked, so J- and L-cuts stay in sync through edits; Attach Audio puts them back.

Filmstrips and waveforms, a frame-accurate ruler, JKL shuttle, snapping, markers (chapter flag), an in/out range, loop, clip names and colour labels, a second Preview Window for another display, Preview Quality Full/Half/Quarter, scrub audio.
Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point. A refused edit says the rule's own sentence.
limits: There is no magnetic or storyline mode; an overlap automatically becomes a cross dissolve.
Markers exist only on the top-level timeline, and a marker's colour can be set only by an agent.
Timeline zoom has no keyboard shortcut except ⇧Z (fit).

capabilities: Move, scale, rotate and crop on the canvas, with snapping to edges, centres and thirds; safe-area guides (90/80 %).
Opacity, 8 blend modes, corner radius, drop shadow, reflection, up to 4 filters (blur, sharpen, pixelate, sepia, noir, vignette, invert).
Chroma key with Pick from Canvas, tolerance, softness and spill.
Spotlight: dim outside a rectangle or ellipse, with optional magnify. Obscure: up to 4 blurred or pixelated regions per clip for privacy, drawn on the canvas.

Text clips with any installed font plus 7 bundled faces, outline, backdrop, auto or fixed-width box, Typewriter/Word Fade/Line Rise reveals, inline canvas editing, and 4 presets (Title, Subtitle, Lower Third, Caption).
Shape clips: rectangle, ellipse, line, arrow, with linear or radial gradients up to 8 stops.
Backgrounds: solid, image, or Add Blurred Background (a blurred fill copy, the vertical-video backdrop).
Matte tracks (Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma, Inverted Luma): any clip on the track, including text, shapes, graphics and video, cuts the track behind it.
limits: No pen or bezier mask tool and no per-clip mask; masking means a matte track or a JS graphic drawing a path.
No motion tracking: regions follow the layer's own transform, never what is in the picture.
Scale is uniform for pictures.
Text presets are 4 hard-coded entries (app/Sources/TextPane.swift TextPreset.all); there are no user-saved text styles.

capabilities: Actions: a span on a clip that eases its properties to an end state along a curve (Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out). Almost everything animates: transform, crop, filters, regions, every grade control, every audio setting, text style, graphic properties, and speed (which is how speed ramps work). Colours blend in OKLab.
An action lane on each clip, both on the timeline and in the Clip tab, with drag, resize and ◆ ◇ ○ ⊘ row marks.
Zoom to Region (Z) draws a rectangle and makes an eased zoom to it; Zoom Back returns. Both are aimed at screencasts.
Motion presets: In and Out (Fade, Zoom In/Out, 4 slides, Spin, Pop) and During (Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce, Drift), tied to the clip's ends.

13 transitions (cross dissolve, fade through black or white, 4 pushes, 5 wipes, slide, zoom) with curve, crossfade on/off and 4 crossfade shapes. Clip ▸ Transition at a hard cut builds the overlap from unused handles.
limits: No independent keyframe track per property, no graph or bezier easing editor, and actions on one clip cannot overlap.
Shape styling, ducking, fade shapes, the voice effect, and track volume/pan cannot be animated.
No motion blur and no auto-animate.

capabilities: Constant speed ×0.1 to ×1000, Fit to a length, ⌥-drag rate stretch, Keep pitch, reverse (rendered in the background), freeze frame.
Speed ramps as actions; Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… gives Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip and Speed Burst in one step. Ramp audio is rendered offline. Captions follow speed changes.
limits: No optical-flow or frame-blend slow motion (frames are repeated or dropped).
Audio is dropped above ×12.
Keep pitch on a ramp can lag up to about 22 ms after a deep slow-down.

capabilities: A per-clip chain: voice isolation (Apple AUSoundIsolation, which also de-reverbs), 16 voice effects, channel pick, 7-slot EQ with voice presets, hum removal, noise reduction, gate, phrase-by-phrase leveller, de-esser, compressor, pan/mono, true-peak limiter, fades in 4 shapes, and a draggable volume line. All of it animates with actions.

Enhance Voice sets a whole voice chain from the clip's own measurements in one step; it can also run automatically when a recording lands. Match Audio copies loudness and speech EQ tone from a reference clip. Normalize goes to LUFS (−16 default) or to peak.
Ducking by clip length or by detected speech (pre-roll and hold).
Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by sound: MFCC speech matching, GCC-PHAT refinement, drift correction by tiny varispeed, and a weak-match confirmation sheet.
Track compressor and limiter (exact in export, approximate in preview); live loudness meter (momentary, short-term, integrated, true peak); scrub audio.
Export always passes a −1 dBTP true-peak master limiter; loudness targets −14, −16, −23 or custom; stems per track or per track name; 24-bit WAV/AIFF.
limits: No beat detection or music retime (#415, #416), no source separation (#417), no AI speech or TTS (#418), no spectrum analyser (#421), no hosting of third-party Audio Units.
No music or SFX library.
Voice isolation and voice effects play only on ×1 clips.
Only the first audio track of a multitrack file is used.

capabilities: Remove Silences: on-device Silero VAD (voice mode) or a level threshold, measured in the mix; it previews the cuts and makes them as one ripple across unlocked tracks.
Remove Filler Words: um/uh and the like cut on AssemblyAI word timings, widened to a 32 ms grid, one undo step. Captions never show fillers.
get_transcript: any clip's timed words (cached cloud transcript or on-device recogniser, cached per media). The Assistant uses it to cut false starts on request.
detect_silence and detect_fillers plus ripple_delete_ranges are exposed to agents.
limits: No text-editor transcript view where deleting words cuts the video; transcript cutting exists only through the Assistant or MCP.
Filler removal is cloud-only: on-device transcription kept 1 of 8 fillers in the owner's test (TR-7).
Cuts never reach into nests or transition overlaps.

capabilities: Generate Captions on this Mac (any installed Speech language, nothing uploaded, model downloadable in the sheet) or with AssemblyAI (BYO key, auto-detect plus 21 languages, speaker labels, vocabulary, cost estimate shown before upload, transcript cache, the service asked to delete its copy).

Two-line Subtitles, or 5 word-by-word short-form styles (Highlight, Pill, Karaoke, Build, One Word) sized to the shorter canvas side, with looks (Slide the pill, Fill words as spoken, Dim in pauses). Restyle with Replace reuses the cached transcript.
Captions are ordinary text clips and are burned in. Import SRT; export SRT or WebVTT per track, round-trip exact to the frame.
limits: No translation or dubbing (no Translation framework import); one language per run.
No soft-subtitle track in exported movies; WebVTT import is not supported.

No keyword emphasis, emoji or animated-emoji captions. Word-style colours have no inspector UI (agent set_text only). Speaker colours apply to Subtitles only, and speakers cannot be named (#192 icebox).

areas.area: Colour grading, HDR and colour management
capabilities: Color tab: Light (exposure, white balance and more), Color, Lift/Gamma/Gain wheels, curves (RGB plus Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat), 8 built-in looks, .cube LUT import, adjustment clips with HSL qualifiers (blur, Show Selection), Show Ungraded, scopes (waveform, parade, vectorscope with zoom, histogram). Every grade control animates.
Sources are read as what they are: iPhone HLG, HDR10/PQ with its peak, wide-gamut SDR. Camera log curves: Apple Log and Apple Log 2 (auto-detected), S-Log3, V-Log, C-Log2/3, or your own LUT.
SDR (Rec. 709) or HDR (HLG) projects; HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables; Show SDR Version preview; opt-in linear-light blending; a 16-bit float compositor.
limits: No Dolby Vision output; no Offset wheel and no qualifier on picture clips (owner closed both as not wanted).
Only Apple Log is detected on import; S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log must be chosen by hand (#278).
No AI or auto colour match between cameras, and no shot-match.

capabilities: A graphic clip is a sandboxed QuickJS module that returns SVG per frame, rasterised by resvg. Properties become inspector controls and animate with actions.

23 bundled templates in the Graphic browser with a live looping preview: bar, line and donut charts; gauge, countdown, counter, progress bar; screencast arrow highlight, callout, keyboard keys, step badge, window frame; chapter card, kinetic type, logo reveal, lower third, news ticker, quote card, title card; social end screen, handle tag, social popup, subscribe button.
Share as a .fjgraphic package with only the fonts and pictures it uses; import by double-click. Agents can write, render (contact sheets) and place modules.
Graphics are prefetched on spare cores, background-rendered when idle, and capped at a quarter of RAM.
limits: A graphic cannot read video pixels (#251 icebox); video shows inside a graphic only through a matte track.
A heavy scene's first play falls behind: resvg takes about 279 ms per 1080p frame (#328, parked).
8-bit rasters (#374).
There is no visual template editor; a new graphic means JavaScript, or asking an agent.

capabilities: Records a display or one window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, the microphone as a separate file auto-aligned, click rings, 30/60 fps, points or pixels, and pause/resume as separate stretches. It lands in a new project or at the playhead of an open one.
Camera alone, or beside the screen as a bottom-right talking-head track (Continuity Camera supported, format picker, live preview).
Microphone-only voice-over at the playhead; 'Enhance the microphone when it lands'.
record_screen over MCP.

capabilities: H.264, HEVC 8-bit, 10-bit and with alpha; AV1 in MP4 or WebM (bundled SVT-AV1, 10-bit, HDR, 3 speeds, time estimate); VP9 WebM and VP9 with alpha (bundled libvpx, Opus audio); ProRes 422/4444; M4A, WAV and AIFF with stems; GIF and APNG; still frames as PNG, JPEG or HEIC.

Size rows follow the document's shape (a vertical 1080p is 1080×1920); quality tiers scaled from area and frame rate; loudness targets; burned-in timecode for review; saved presets; an Export Queue that runs while you keep editing, with a memory ledger for software encoders.
Chapter markers become embedded chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM. MP4 is written fast-start.

capabilities: The whole editor as MCP tools over a local Unix socket: one tool per core op (64 op tools) plus app-state tools, 106 product tools in all (per CLAUDE.md). The bundled framejob-mcp stdio helper launches the app on first call; Settings has a one-click 'Copy MCP Command' for Claude Code.
render_frame lets an agent look at frames, including scope data; get_project returns the whole project JSON; every agent edit is a normal undo step, shown live in the window.

An in-app Assistant (Claude, BYO Anthropic key) in an inspector tab. A built-in Claude Assistant on the user's own key that uses the same tools, renders frames to check visual edits, asks before writing files, withholds cloud uploads and recording, and shows per-turn and monthly cost.

A built-in recorder (screen, window, camera beside the screen, voice-over) feeding straight into the timeline, plus screencast tools: Zoom to Region, spotlight, obscure regions, and screencast graphics.

A programmable motion-graphics engine: JS modules drawing SVG per frame, 23 templates, properties as inspector controls and animatable, shareable .fjgraphic packages, and agents that can write new graphics on demand.

A serious colour and HDR pipeline in a creator app: log curves for Apple, Sony, Panasonic and Canon; HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables; a 16-bit float compositor; wheels, curves, hue curves, qualifiers, adjustment clips, LUTs, four scopes.
Codec breadth: bundled SVT-AV1 and libvpx (AV1 in MP4 and WebM, VP9 and VP9-with-alpha WebM for transparent web video), HEVC with alpha, ProRes 4444, APNG; WebM and MKV import without re-encode.
Word-by-word social captions (5 styles plus looks) on-device or via AssemblyAI with cost estimates and transcript caching; transcript-timed filler removal.
A native Swift/AppKit app with a Rust core, deterministic preview/export parity, and an unusually large automated proof suite.

Assistant guardrails by design: it never records, never closes its own project, never starts paid cloud transcription, and asks before writing exports or saves.

Track compressor and limiter (exact in export, approximate in preview); live loudness meter (momentary, short-term, integrated, true peak); scrub audio.

A serious colour and HDR pipeline in a creator app: log curves for Apple, Sony, Panasonic and Canon; HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables; a 16-bit float compositor; wheels, curves, hue curves, qualifiers, adjustment clips, LUTs, four scopes.

A native Swift/AppKit app with a Rust core, deterministic preview/export parity, and an unusually large automated proof suite.
